nodes.name: Isis
nodes.significant_event: Resurrects Osiris; mother of Horus; her name means 'seat/throne'
nodes.symbolism: Throne as 'seat' - the mother is the throne that makes the king; combines features of Terrible and Good Mother; Stella Maris (Star of the Sea)
nodes.neumann_archetype: Central archetype combining Terrible and Good Mother. Corresponds to the full Great Mother archetype.

nodes.name: Demeter
nodes.domain: agriculture, grain, fertility, motherhood, the Eleusinian Mysteries, seasons, law
nodes.object: sheaf of wheat, torch, scepter, cornucopia
nodes.character_trait: grieving, nourishing, life-giving, wrathful when wronged, lawgiving
nodes.physical_characteristics: mature, beautiful woman, often veiled or crowned with grain, carrying a torch
nodes.significant_event: searches desperately for her abducted daughter Persephone, causes universal famine until Persephone is returned, establishes the Eleusinian Mysteries, pig sacrificed in Thesmophoria festival
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughter of the Titans Cronus and Rhea, swallowed by Cronus at birth and later disgorged
nodes.symbolism: the grieving mother, death and rebirth of vegetation, the Eleusinian mystery of grain that dies in earth and is reborn, the mother-daughter bond as the deepest human relationship
nodes.neumann_archetype: the positive pole of the Great Mother (M+), the nourishing earth goddess whose loss of the daughter represents the mysteries of death and regeneration

nodes.name: Sophia
nodes.significant_event: Projection of the Good Mother archetype; Sophia-virgin as positive anima
nodes.symbolism: Good Mother projection; positive anima figure; represents wisdom and spiritual transformation; counterpart to Gorgon
nodes.neumann_archetype: Represents the Good Mother projection, the positive pole of the Archetypal Feminine.

nodes.name: Uroboros
nodes.domain: creation, eternity, cyclical renewal, primordial chaos
nodes.physical_characteristics: serpent or dragon devouring its own tail, forming a circle
nodes.significant_event: appears in ancient Egyptian funerary texts as symbol of the sun cycle, adopted across Greek alchemy and Norse cosmology as Jormungandr
nodes.birth_circumstances: primordial symbol predating individual mythological traditions
nodes.symbolism: eternal cyclic renewal, unity of creation and destruction, the Great Round preceding all differentiation, wholeness containing all opposites
nodes.neumann_archetype: the Great Round preceding all differentiation, contains both masculine and feminine, precedes the separation of the World Parents

nodes.name: Osiris
nodes.significant_event: Embraced by cedar tree; djed pillar as coffin; religion of Osiris and Horus promises rebirth to all souls
nodes.symbolism: Djed pillar is both phallic-masculine and containing-feminine; cedar tree embraces corpse as earth-womb; promises universal rebirth
nodes.neumann_archetype: His djed pillar is both masculine and feminine-containing. The cedar tree embracing his corpse represents the earth-womb.

nodes.name: Tiamat
nodes.domain: sea, prophecy, creation, motherhood, chaos, fate
nodes.significant_event: Defeated by Marduk; body split to form heaven and earth; 'mother of the gods and possessor of the table of fate'
nodes.symbolism: Male-female uroboric unity with Apsu; primordial chaos of water; mother of all gods; split body becomes heaven and earth
nodes.neumann_archetype: Key example of the uroboric Great Mother. Constitutes primordial male-female unity with Apsu.

nodes.name: Gorgon
nodes.character_trait: terrifying, petrifying, protective when controlled, primal
nodes.physical_characteristics: female face with serpent hair, tusks, lolling tongue, wide staring eyes, sometimes winged
nodes.significant_event: Medusa the mortal Gorgon was beheaded by Perseus, her head was placed on Athenas aegis as an apotropaic device, the Gorgoneion was used throughout Greek art as a protective emblem
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughters of the sea gods Phorcys and Ceto, the three sisters Stheno, Euryale, and Medusa
nodes.symbolism: the terrifying face of the unconscious feminine, the Gorgoneion as ward against evil by confronting viewers with primal terror, the mask as the boundary between human and monstrous
nodes.neumann_archetype: the Terrible Mother projection, the terrifying aspect of the unconscious feminine at the negative pole (M-), the face that petrifies consciousness

nodes.name: Hathor
nodes.significant_event: Ritual baring before grieving Demeter parallel; nurturing cow of heaven; Isis-Hathor fusion
nodes.symbolism: Nurturing cow of heaven; horns as maternal symbols; fused with Isis as Isis-Hathor; cow-heaven mother
nodes.neumann_archetype: The nurturing cow of heaven. Associated with both terrible and positive aspects. Fused with Isis.

nodes.name: Nut
nodes.significant_event: Embraces the dead on sarcophagi for rebirth; heavenly cow who waters earth with rain-milk
nodes.symbolism: Celestial goddess; symbol of femininity; Lady of Heaven; goddess of rebirth but also death as Nuit
nodes.neumann_archetype: Celestial vessel-goddess. 'Goddess of rebirth, but she also has the character of death as Nuit.'

nodes.name: Artemis
nodes.domain: hunt, wilderness, moon, childbirth, virginity, wild animals
nodes.object: bow, arrow, quiver, hunting spear, crescent moon
nodes.animals: deer, bear, hunting dog, boar, quail
nodes.character_trait: virginal, fierce, independent, protective of the wild, punishing
nodes.physical_characteristics: tall, athletic, youthful huntress in short tunic, many-breasted in Ephesian form
nodes.significant_event: protects her virginity fiercely, transforms Actaeon into a stag for seeing her bathe, demands sacrifice of Iphigenia at Aulis, punishes Niobe for boasting
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughter of Zeus and Leto, twin sister of Apollo, born on the island of Delos where she assisted her mothers delivery of Apollo
nodes.symbolism: the untamed feminine, wilderness as sacred space, virginity as autonomous power rather than passivity, the Great Goddess in her aspect as Lady of the Beasts
nodes.neumann_archetype: the virginal Great Goddess encompassing all poles, the non-Greek Artemis is broader than the classical virginal version, includes Hecate-Artemis cult

nodes.name: Madonna
nodes.significant_event: Pieta (holding dead Jesus); Stella Maris (Star of the Sea); spinner of fate
nodes.symbolism: Stella Maris paralleling Isis and Tara; Pieta as mother of death; Christian continuation of Great Mother; spinner of fate
nodes.neumann_archetype: Christian continuation of Great Mother archetype. Stella Maris paralleling Isis and Tara.

nodes.name: Lady of the Beasts
nodes.domain: hunt, wild animals, wilderness, fertility, sovereignty over nature
nodes.character_trait: wild, primordial, sovereign, untamed, protective of animals
nodes.physical_characteristics: female figure flanked by animals, often winged, grasping beasts in each hand
nodes.significant_event: depicted on Minoan seals and Greek pottery as Potnia Theron, identified with Artemis and Circe in Homer
nodes.birth_circumstances: Neolithic and Bronze Age archetype surviving into classical mythology
nodes.symbolism: primordial feminine sovereignty over the animal world, the Great Goddess in her aspect as mistress of nature, predating Olympian religion
nodes.neumann_archetype: ancient form of the Great Goddess predating differentiated pantheons, the feminine as sovereign over all living things

nodes.name: Quetzalcoatl
nodes.domain: wisdom, storm, rebirth, light, sacrifice, souls, creation
nodes.significant_event: Inner spiritual transformation; identical with morning star; god of winds; son deity
nodes.symbolism: Name combines quetzalli 'tail feather' and coatl 'serpent'; highest form of spiritual hero myth; inner transformation
nodes.neumann_archetype: Highest form of the hero myth achieving spiritual self-transformation.

nodes.name: Odin
nodes.domain: war, death, wisdom, prophecy, music, fate
nodes.significant_event: Hanging from Yggdrasil; takes wisdom from volvas (seeresses); relation to Mimir's spring
nodes.symbolism: Bond with spring of fate; judgment seat at world ash tree; takes wisdom from feminine seeresses
nodes.neumann_archetype: Takes wisdom from feminine seeresses. His hanging from Yggdrasil reflects relation to tree of fate.

nodes.name: Hecate
nodes.domain: magic, witchcraft, crossroads, ghosts, the moon, necromancy, entrance ways
nodes.animals: dog, polecat, red mullet, serpent, horse
nodes.character_trait: terrible, dark, liminal, powerful, mysterious, generous to her devotees
nodes.physical_characteristics: triple-formed, carrying torches, accompanied by howling dogs, appears at crossroads at night
nodes.significant_event: assisted Demeter in searching for Persephone with her torches, retains cosmic power even under Zeus rule according to Hesiod, worshipped at crossroads with offerings of food
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughter of the Titans Perses and Asteria, honored by Zeus above all other gods according to Hesiod
nodes.symbolism: the liminal spaces between worlds, the terrible aspect of the feminine that rules night and death, crossroads as places of choice and danger, magic as feminine knowledge
nodes.neumann_archetype: the Terrible Mother at the negative pole (M-), the dark moon goddess fused with Artemis representing the full range of the Great Goddess from nurturing to terrifying

nodes.name: Ra
nodes.significant_event: Born from Neith without father; son of heavenly cow goddess; Ammon-Ra as creator
nodes.symbolism: Sun god born from self-generating mother Neith; endangered son protected by cow goddess recitations
nodes.neumann_archetype: Born from self-generating mother. The heavenly cow goddess composed recitations for her endangered son Ra.

nodes.name: Tara
nodes.physical_characteristics: green or white, seated in lotus, crowned, youthful
nodes.significant_event: 'Mistress of boats, capable of pacifying the watery flood'; savioress; 'the wise worship me as Tara'
nodes.symbolism: Great Good Goddess; Stella Maris parallel to Madonna and Isis; 'redeeming one' (Tarini)
nodes.neumann_archetype: Great Good Goddess paralleling Madonna and Isis as Stella Maris.

nodes.name: Venus
nodes.significant_event: Venus of Willendorf; Lespugne Venus; earliest Great Mother representations
nodes.symbolism: Paleolithic fertility figurines; exaggerated hips, breasts, belly; earliest known Great Mother representations
nodes.neumann_archetype: Earliest prehistoric representations of the Great Mother archetype (Venus figurines).

nodes.name: Norns
nodes.significant_event: Spin and twist thread of fate; third breaks it off; shape hero's fate at night
nodes.symbolism: Triple fate goddesses; spinning and breaking thread of destiny; past-present-future; birth-life-death
nodes.neumann_archetype: Two spin and twist thread, third breaks it off. Represent beginning-middle-end, past-present-future.

nodes.name: Ishtar
nodes.significant_event: Descent to underworld; terrible and positive aspects
nodes.symbolism: Great Goddess combining terrible and positive; creatress as potter (Mama/Aruru); with branches/ears of grain
nodes.neumann_archetype: Both terrible and positive. At negative pole as terrible Ishtar, but also Great Goddess encompassing multiple aspects.

nodes.name: Dionysus
nodes.domain: wine, ecstasy, theater, fertility, ritual madness, death and rebirth, vegetation
nodes.object: thyrsus, wine cup, ivy crown, grapevine, mask
nodes.animals: bull, goat, panther, leopard, serpent, dolphin, donkey
nodes.character_trait: ecstatic, transformative, dangerous, liberating, maddening, joyful
nodes.physical_characteristics: effeminate, beautiful, sometimes bearded and robed, sometimes youthful and androgynous, crowned with ivy
nodes.significant_event: establishes his cult across Greece against opposition, drives resisters mad, descends to the underworld to rescue his mother Semele, reconciled with Apollo at Delphi
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of Zeus and the mortal Semele, born from Zeus thigh after Semele was destroyed by Zeus thunderbolt, in Orphic tradition torn apart as Zagreus and reborn
nodes.symbolism: the dissolution of individual identity in ecstasy, the dying and rising god of vegetation, the union of civilization and wildness, wine as divine madness
nodes.neumann_archetype: the ecstatic-matriarchal realm, the son-lover of the Great Mother who dies and is reborn, his opposition to Apollo is superficial as both are reconciled at Delphi

nodes.name: Horus
nodes.significant_event: Son of Isis; infant nursed by mother; king through the mother
nodes.symbolism: Divine child of the Great Mother; 'through whom alone he is king'; divine child archetype
nodes.neumann_archetype: Son of Isis. The king is Horus through the mother. Represents the divine child archetype.

nodes.name: Kali
nodes.object: skulls, severed heads, hands, necklace of skulls
nodes.significant_event: Blood sacrifices at Kalighat (Calcutta); ~800 goats sacrificed at Durgapuja
nodes.symbolism: Terrible Mother archetype; 'dark, all-devouring time'; stands on Shiva's corpse; devouring feminine
nodes.neumann_archetype: Primary example of the Terrible Mother. 'Dark, all-devouring time.' Stands on Shiva's corpse.

nodes.name: Aphrodite
nodes.domain: love, beauty, desire, sexuality, war, seafaring
nodes.physical_characteristics: golden, irresistibly beautiful, naked or lightly robed, born from sea foam
nodes.significant_event: Also goddess of war in Sparta and Cyprus; enchants and ruins men
nodes.birth_circumstances: born from the sea foam that gathered around the severed genitals of Uranus cast into the sea by Cronus
nodes.symbolism: irresistible desire, beauty as both creative and destructive force, the power of sexuality over gods and mortals alike
nodes.neumann_archetype: the Transformative Feminine as enchantress, the anima figure who enchants and ruins through desire

nodes.name: Maya
nodes.significant_event: World as Maya/illusion; as Heimarmene/fate; as monster or witch
nodes.symbolism: Cosmic illusion; world as hell or Maya; fate as Heimarmene; goddess as the Maya, 'the great...'
nodes.neumann_archetype: The goddess as Maya, cosmic illusion and fate.

nodes.name: Eve
nodes.domain: creation, motherhood, first pair of humans
nodes.significant_event: Taken from Adam (unnatural symbol); Jewish life-affirming aspect
nodes.symbolism: Unnatural origin from Adam reverses natural birth; 'the naked Eve. Her belly is life'; resembles Astarte and Gaea
nodes.neumann_archetype: Her origin from Adam is an 'unnatural symbol.' In Jewish aspect, life-affirming.

nodes.name: Huitzilopochtli
nodes.significant_event: Son of Coatlicue; Aztec war/sun god requiring human sacrifice
nodes.symbolism: Hero god of the Aztecs; son of earth mother Coatlicue; sun warrior deity
nodes.neumann_archetype: Aztec hero/war god, son of Coatlicue the earth mother.

nodes.name: Sphinx
nodes.domain: death, riddles, protection, wisdom through terror
nodes.character_trait: enigmatic, deadly, self-destroying when defeated, guardian
nodes.physical_characteristics: lion body, human head, eagle wings, sometimes serpents tail
nodes.significant_event: sat outside Thebes posing a riddle to all who passed and devouring those who failed, killed herself when Oedipus answered correctly
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughter of Typhon and Echidna, or of Orthos and the Chimera
nodes.symbolism: the enigma of human identity (What walks on four legs, two legs, three legs?), the monstrous guardian who tests consciousness, the riddle as threshold between ignorance and knowledge
nodes.neumann_archetype: the guardian figure at the threshold of consciousness, the veiled sphinx with penetrating eyes who tests the hero, connected to the motherhood-death duality

nodes.name: Mary
nodes.significant_event: Heaven goes under robe of Mary; upper and lower feminine principles kindled
nodes.symbolism: Upper and lower feminine principles; Holy Ghost connection; continuation of Great Mother in Christianity
nodes.neumann_archetype: Christian continuation of the Great Mother. Upper and lower feminine principles kindled through Mary.

nodes.name: Nekhbet
nodes.significant_event: Vulture goddess of south; Great Goddess of Upper Egypt
nodes.symbolism: Vulture symbolizes death and rebirth; 'white-crowned Great Goddess of Upper Egypt'
nodes.neumann_archetype: Vulture goddess symbolizing death and rebirth. Great Goddess of Upper Egypt.

nodes.name: Persephone (Kore)
nodes.domain: underworld, spring, vegetation, death and rebirth, the Eleusinian Mysteries
nodes.object: pomegranate, torch, sheaf of grain, narcissus flower
nodes.character_trait: innocent, transformative, dual-natured, regal, maiden and queen
nodes.physical_characteristics: youthful and beautiful as Kore, regal and fearsome as Queen of the Underworld
nodes.significant_event: abducted by Hades while gathering flowers, ate pomegranate seeds in the underworld binding her to spend part of each year below, her annual return brings spring
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughter of Zeus and Demeter
nodes.symbolism: the seed that must descend into the earth to be reborn, the maiden who becomes queen of death, the mother-daughter unity of Demeter-Kore as the deepest mystery of Eleusis
nodes.neumann_archetype: daughter and partial figure of Demeter, the Kore who descends to become queen of the underworld, representing the corn mothers seed returning to earth

nodes.name: Mayauel
nodes.significant_event: Goddess of intoxicant from maguey; Mexican Great Goddess
nodes.symbolism: 400 breasts = superabundant nourishment; stars in celestial ocean; parallel to Diana of Ephesus
nodes.neumann_archetype: Mexican Great Goddess with 400 breasts, symbolizing superabundant nourishment.

nodes.name: Hel
nodes.significant_event: Rules the Norse underworld
nodes.symbolism: Terrible Mother as ruler of the dead; Norse underworld goddess
nodes.neumann_archetype: Norse death goddess representing the Terrible Mother as ruler of the underworld.

nodes.name: Adonis
nodes.domain: love, beauty, vegetation, death and rebirth
nodes.physical_characteristics: extraordinarily beautiful young man, youthful and desirable
nodes.significant_event: Born from tree; mourned with breast-beating; seed grain symbolism
nodes.birth_circumstances: born from the myrrh tree into which his mother Myrrha had been transformed after an incestuous union with her father Cinyras
nodes.symbolism: Born from tree like vegetation gods; ritual breast-beating mourning; seed grain taken to underworld and reborn
nodes.neumann_archetype: Born from tree. Mourned with ritual breast-beating. Represents vegetation death-rebirth cycle.

nodes.name: Gaea
nodes.physical_characteristics: emerges from the earth itself, sometimes depicted as a matronly woman rising from the ground
nodes.significant_event: bore Uranus and mated with him to produce the Titans, urged Cronus to castrate Uranus, later sent the Giants and Typhon against Zeus
nodes.birth_circumstances: self-born from Chaos at the beginning of creation according to Hesiod
nodes.symbolism: the primordial earth from which all life springs, the Great Mother who both creates and threatens the patriarchal order, the earth as living maternal body
nodes.neumann_archetype: the primordial Great Mother preceding all differentiation, the earth goddess linked to Eve and Astarte

nodes.name: Diana of Ephesus
nodes.domain: fertility, nature, nourishment, the cosmos, beasts
nodes.character_trait: all-nourishing, cosmic, encompassing, mother of all
nodes.physical_characteristics: many-breasted or adorned with multiple egg-shaped protuberances, crowned with a city-wall crown, adorned with zodiac beasts
nodes.significant_event: her temple at Ephesus was one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, her cult attracted devotees from across the ancient world
nodes.birth_circumstances: ancient Anatolian mother goddess syncretized with Greek Artemis
nodes.symbolism: cosmic nourishment through the divine feminine, the Great Goddess adorned with the signs of the zodiac representing universal sustenance
nodes.neumann_archetype: the classical form of the nourishing Great Goddess, cosmic nourishment expressed through zodiac beast adornment

nodes.name: Neith
nodes.significant_event: Brought forth son Ra without husband; part of quaternary with Hathor, Bast
nodes.symbolism: Unitary world of the Archetypal Feminine; self-generating mother; bore Ra without male aid
nodes.neumann_archetype: Represents the unitary world of the Archetypal Feminine. Self-generating.

nodes.name: Apollo
nodes.domain: sun, prophecy, music, poetry, healing, plague, archery, order, truth
nodes.animals: swan, raven, dolphin, wolf, mouse, python
nodes.character_trait: rational, orderly, beautiful, truthful, sometimes cruel, far-striking
nodes.significant_event: Opposition to Dionysus at Delphi; Pythian Apollo
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of Zeus and the Titaness Leto, twin brother of Artemis, born on the island of Delos
nodes.symbolism: rational consciousness, the light of truth and order, the tension between civilization and ecstatic experience, prophecy as divine knowledge
nodes.neumann_archetype: the solar hero representing the triumph of consciousness over the unconscious, opposed to and reconciled with Dionysus at Delphi

nodes.name: Marduk
nodes.significant_event: Defeats Tiamat; creates heaven and earth from her body
nodes.symbolism: Patriarchal sun god who defeats uroboric mother; creates ordered world from chaos
nodes.neumann_archetype: Patriarchal sun god who defeats Tiamat, splitting her body to create heaven and earth.

nodes.name: Bast
nodes.significant_event: Part of quaternary with Hathor, Neith
nodes.symbolism: Part of Egyptian goddess quaternary; paired with Neith
nodes.neumann_archetype: Part of the quaternary with Hathor and Neith in the Archetypal Feminine.

nodes.name: Circe
nodes.character_trait: enchanting, powerful, dangerous, knowledgeable, seductive, ultimately helpful
nodes.physical_characteristics: beautiful goddess with braided hair, singing at her loom, surrounded by enchanted beasts
nodes.significant_event: transforms Odysseus men into swine, is overcome by Odysseus with Hermes help, becomes his lover and advisor, directs him to the underworld to consult Tiresias
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughter of the sun god Helios and the Oceanid Perse, sister of King Aeetes of Colchis, aunt of Medea
nodes.symbolism: the enchantress who transforms men into beasts, the feminine power that can either bestialize or enlighten, the Lady of the Beasts in the Odyssey
nodes.neumann_archetype: personalized form of primordial enchantment, the Aphrodite-like figure always subject to defeat by the conscious hero, the Lady of the Beasts who transforms the unworthy

nodes.name: Cybele
nodes.domain: earth, nature, motherhood, fertility, wild animals, mountains
nodes.object: tympanum, mural crown, libation bowl, chariot
nodes.physical_characteristics: seated, crowned with city walls, robed
nodes.significant_event: Stone of Pessinus moved to Rome; strangled victims as Gorgon
nodes.symbolism: Mother Goddess who 'strangled them as Gorgon, as Cybele'; stone cult; from Pessinus to Rome
nodes.neumann_archetype: Mother Goddess who 'strangled them as Gorgon, as Cybele.'

nodes.name: Zeus
nodes.domain: sky, thunder, lightning, kingship, justice, cosmic order, hospitality, oaths
nodes.character_trait: sovereign, powerful, patriarchal, just, amorous, wrathful, protective of order
nodes.physical_characteristics: tall, bearded, majestic, enthroned, wielding thunderbolt
nodes.significant_event: overthrew his father Cronus and the Titans in the Titanomachy, divided the cosmos with his brothers Poseidon and Hades, established divine and human law from Olympus
nodes.birth_circumstances: youngest son of Cronus and Rhea, hidden in Crete by his mother to escape being swallowed, raised on honey and goats milk in a cave
nodes.symbolism: divine sovereignty and cosmic order, the sky father who maintains justice, the tension between absolute power and moral law, honey as purest product of nature nourishing the infant god
nodes.neumann_archetype: the patriarchal sky god who inherits and divides the Great Mothers realms with his brothers, fed with honey as newborn representing natures purest essence

nodes.name: Ceres
nodes.significant_event: Ceres-Spes (Hope) association; bee symbolism; Cretan Great Goddess connection
nodes.symbolism: Ceres-Spes (Hope); bee association with moon; Cretan Great Goddess; Demeter parallel
nodes.neumann_archetype: Roman Demeter. Associated with Spes (Hope) and the Cretan Great Goddess.

nodes.name: Astarte
nodes.object: star, horned crown, sphinx, shield, spear
nodes.significant_event: Widely distributed 'Astarte type'; figure resembling Eve, Astarte, and Gaea
nodes.symbolism: Fatal enchantment; 'Astarte type' with hands on breasts; linked to Eve and Gaea
nodes.neumann_archetype: Figure of fatal enchantment. The widely distributed 'Astarte type.'

nodes.name: Baubo
nodes.domain: fertility, obscenity, humor, the body, ritual laughter
nodes.physical_characteristics: belly as face, legs as chin, vulva as mouth, or simply a woman lifting her skirt
nodes.significant_event: lifted her skirts to expose herself before the grieving Demeter, making the goddess laugh and breaking her fast during the search for Persephone, Priene terracotta figurines depict her
nodes.birth_circumstances: Eleusinian figure, wife of Dysaules, or old servant woman
nodes.symbolism: the sacred obscenity that defeats grief, the belly and genitals as the creative center of the feminine, ritual laughter as restoration of life force
nodes.neumann_archetype: the belly character of the woman, ritual baring and obscenity as life-affirming, the feminine body as source of laughter and renewed vitality against death

nodes.name: Hermes
nodes.domain: travel, commerce, trickery, communication, boundaries, souls, thieves, language
nodes.object: caduceus, winged sandals, winged helmet, lyre, shepherds crook
nodes.character_trait: clever, cunning, liminal, guiding, inventive, eloquent, mischievous
nodes.physical_characteristics: youthful, athletic, beardless in later art, winged sandals and hat, carrying caduceus
nodes.significant_event: stole Apollos cattle on the day he was born, invented the lyre from a tortoise shell, guided souls to the underworld as psychopomp, slew the hundred-eyed giant Argus
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of Zeus and the Pleiad Maia, born in a cave on Mount Cyllene in Arcadia
nodes.symbolism: the crossing of all boundaries, communication between divine and human realms, the psychopomp who guides between life and death, trickery as creative intelligence
nodes.neumann_archetype: the soul-guide (Seelenfuhrer) who mediates between consciousness and the unconscious, the snake-entwined healing staff connecting the worlds

nodes.name: Shiva
nodes.significant_event: Kali stands on Shiva's corpse; Shiva or Shakti contained in double symbol; 'the imperturbable'
nodes.symbolism: Kali stands on his corpse; 'double symbol in which Shiva or Shakti is contained'; 'the imperturbable'
nodes.neumann_archetype: Kali stands on his corpse. 'The imperturbable' contained within Shakti.

nodes.name: Scylla
nodes.physical_characteristics: twelve feet, six long necks with fearsome heads each containing three rows of teeth, a belt of dog heads around her waist
nodes.significant_event: devoured six of Odysseus sailors as his ship passed through the strait between her and Charybdis, no hero could defeat her
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughter of Phorcys and Hecate or Crataiis, or transformed from a beautiful nymph by Circe
nodes.symbolism: the inescapable peril that must be endured, the devouring feminine from which there is no escape, the monstrous transformation of beauty
nodes.neumann_archetype: the devouring female figure at the negative pole of the Great Mother, alluring and death-dealing, whose mother is connected to the underworld

nodes.name: Eumenides
nodes.domain: vengeance, blood guilt, justice, oaths, the underworld
nodes.character_trait: relentless, implacable, just, terrifying, ancient, earth-connected
nodes.physical_characteristics: snake-haired, black-robed, weeping tears of blood, carrying torches and whips
nodes.significant_event: pursued Orestes for the murder of his mother Clytemnestra, transformed into the Eumenides (Kindly Ones) by Athena at the trial on the Areopagus in Aeschylus Oresteia
nodes.birth_circumstances: born from the blood of Uranus that fell on Gaia when Cronus castrated him, or daughters of Nyx
nodes.symbolism: the ancient chthonic law of blood vengeance, the transition from vendetta to civic justice, the earth-connected feminine powers older than the Olympians
nodes.neumann_archetype: the chthonic sisters of the Great Mother representing the inescapable law of the earth, receiving offerings characteristic of earth goddesses

nodes.name: Valkyrie
nodes.significant_event: Choose the slain; associated with waelcyrge
nodes.symbolism: Death-bringing feminine warrior; waelcyrge (chooser of the slain); associated with ravens and fate
nodes.neumann_archetype: Death-bringing feminine warrior. Waelcyrge (chooser of slain) connects to fate.

nodes.name: Medusa
nodes.physical_characteristics: snake-haired, with tusks, lolling tongue, wide staring eyes that turn onlookers to stone
nodes.significant_event: transformed from a beautiful maiden into a monster by Athena for being violated by Poseidon in Athenas temple, beheaded by Perseus, from her blood sprang Pegasus and Chrysaor
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughter of the sea deities Phorcys and Ceto, the only mortal among the three Gorgon sisters
nodes.symbolism: the petrifying terror of the feminine, the apotropaic face that wards off evil, beauty destroyed and made monstrous, the gaze that freezes consciousness
nodes.neumann_archetype: the Terrible Mother whose petrifying gaze belongs to the province of the negative pole (M-), representing the terrifying aspect of the unconscious feminine

nodes.name: Durga
nodes.significant_event: Durgapuja festival with ~800 goat sacrifices; name means 'Unapproachable'
nodes.symbolism: The 'Unapproachable' and 'Perilous'; Indian Terrible Mother; blood sacrifice
nodes.neumann_archetype: The 'Unapproachable' and 'Perilous.' Indian Terrible Mother requiring blood sacrifice.

nodes.name: Lilith
nodes.significant_event: Mesopotamian goddess of night, evil, death
nodes.symbolism: Specter figure; 'Mesopotamian goddess Lilith of night, evil, and death, winged'
nodes.neumann_archetype: Specter figure. Mesopotamian goddess of night, evil, and death.

nodes.name: Maat
nodes.significant_event: Correlated with Sophia-Wisdom at positive pole
nodes.symbolism: Justice and cosmic order; correlated with Sophia-Wisdom and Kore
nodes.neumann_archetype: Egyptian goddess of justice correlated with Sophia-Wisdom at the positive pole.

nodes.name: Tlazolteotl
nodes.significant_event: Earth goddess of sexuality and purification
nodes.symbolism: Mexican earth/purification goddess; transformation aspect of the Great Mother
nodes.neumann_archetype: Mexican goddess associated with the earth and transformation.

nodes.name: Xochiquetzal
nodes.significant_event: Mexican goddess of beauty and flowers
nodes.symbolism: Mexican flower goddess; beauty and fertility of the Great Mother
nodes.neumann_archetype: Mexican goddess representing the positive, beautiful aspect of the feminine.

nodes.name: Selene
nodes.physical_characteristics: radiant, pale, crowned with crescent moon, driving a chariot across the night sky
nodes.significant_event: fell in love with the mortal shepherd Endymion and asked Zeus to grant him eternal sleep so she could visit him every night, bore him fifty daughters
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughter of the Titans Hyperion and Theia, sister of Helios the sun and Eos the dawn
nodes.symbolism: the eternal feminine cycle, the moon as reflection of the sun, the desire for the beautiful mortal who must sleep to be preserved
nodes.neumann_archetype: the moon goddess as aspect of the Great Goddess, listed alongside Persephone and Medusa as manifestations of the archetypal feminine

nodes.name: Eileithyia
nodes.character_trait: birth-bringing, sometimes obstructing, powerful over labor
nodes.physical_characteristics: woman in labor position, or standing with arms raised, sometimes veiled
nodes.significant_event: Hera sent her to delay the birth of Heracles and hasten the birth of Eurystheus, her Cretan cave cult predates Olympian religion
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughter of Zeus and Hera, or an ancient pre-Olympian Cretan goddess
nodes.symbolism: the divine power over the moment of birth, the feminine mystery of bringing life into the world, the threshold between nonexistence and existence
nodes.neumann_archetype: the birth goddess representing the generative power of the Great Mother, the feminine as the gate through which all life must pass

nodes.name: Asherah
nodes.significant_event: Asherah pole as symbol of Great Mother
nodes.symbolism: Sacred pillar/pole as symbol of Great Mother; tree/pillar feminine symbolism
nodes.neumann_archetype: The asherah pillar is a symbol of the Great Mother.

nodes.name: Chicomecoatl
nodes.significant_event: Mexican corn goddess; 'Seven Serpent'
nodes.symbolism: Mexican corn/vegetation goddess; nourishing aspect of the Great Mother
nodes.neumann_archetype: Mexican corn goddess representing the nourishing vegetation aspect.

nodes.name: Kwan-yin
nodes.object: lotus, water vessel, willow branch, rosary
nodes.significant_event: Listed with Isis, Demeter, Artemis, Ishtar as Great Goddess forms
nodes.symbolism: Buddhist compassion goddess; Chinese Great Goddess paralleling Isis and Demeter
nodes.neumann_archetype: Listed alongside Isis, Demeter, Artemis as forms of the positive Great Mother.

nodes.name: Britomartis
nodes.physical_characteristics: Cretan goddess of wild nature, sweet maiden
nodes.significant_event: pursued by King Minos for nine months, leaped into the sea to escape and was caught in fishermens nets, became an immortal goddess honored by Artemis
nodes.birth_circumstances: Cretan goddess, daughter of Zeus and Carme
nodes.symbolism: the sweet wildness of untamed nature, the maiden who chooses death over submission, the ancient Cretan face of the Great Goddess
nodes.neumann_archetype: paired with Dictynna as an aspect of the Great Goddess, the Cretan maiden-huntress predating classical Artemis

nodes.name: Dictynna
nodes.physical_characteristics: wild huntress associated with nets and the Cretan mountains
nodes.significant_event: leaped from a cliff into the sea to escape King Minos pursuit, caught in fishermens nets, adopted into Artemis cult
nodes.birth_circumstances: Cretan goddess or nymph, sometimes identified with Britomartis
nodes.symbolism: the untamed feminine who would rather die than submit, the net as both capture and salvation, the Cretan origins of the Greek huntress-goddess
nodes.neumann_archetype: aspect of the virginal Great Goddess, the Cretan predecessor of the classical Artemis

nodes.name: Tammuz
nodes.significant_event: Descent to underworld; mourned by Ishtar/Inanna
nodes.symbolism: Dying-and-rising vegetation god; paired with Ishtar/Inanna
nodes.neumann_archetype: Dying-and-rising god paired with Ishtar.

nodes.name: Shakti
nodes.significant_event: Contained within Shiva; cosmic feminine principle
nodes.symbolism: Divine feminine power; 'double symbol in which Shiva or Shakti is contained'
nodes.neumann_archetype: 'Double symbol in which Shiva or Shakti is contained.' Cosmic feminine principle.

nodes.name: Coatlicue
nodes.significant_event: Mother of Huitzilopochtli; Mexican Terrible Mother
nodes.symbolism: Mexican snake goddess; Terrible Mother; earth combining creation and death
nodes.neumann_archetype: Mexican snake goddess representing the Terrible Mother.

nodes.name: Rangda
nodes.physical_characteristics: long hair, fanged, bulging eyes, long tongue, pendulous breasts, clawed
nodes.significant_event: Balinese witch representing the Terrible Mother
nodes.symbolism: Balinese Terrible Mother/witch archetype
nodes.neumann_archetype: Balinese witch representing the Terrible Mother archetype.

nodes.name: Inanna
nodes.significant_event: Descent to underworld; Sumerian precursor to Ishtar
nodes.symbolism: Sumerian Great Goddess; precursor to Ishtar
nodes.neumann_archetype: Sumerian precursor to Babylonian Ishtar.

nodes.name: Attis
nodes.significant_event: Vegetation god associated with Cybele
nodes.death_circumstances: Castrated himself in madness; died; resurrected as a pine tree
nodes.symbolism: Dying-and-rising vegetation god; paired with Cybele
nodes.neumann_archetype: Dying-and-rising vegetation god associated with Cybele.

nodes.name: Fortuna
nodes.significant_event: Parallels Indian/Tibetan Tara
nodes.symbolism: Fate goddess in lion chariot; parallel to Tara; Great Mother as fate
nodes.neumann_archetype: Sat in chariot drawn by lions, paralleling Tara on lion.

nodes.name: Rhea
nodes.domain: fertility, motherhood, generation, mountains, the flow of time
nodes.object: stone wrapped in swaddling clothes, tambourine, crown
nodes.character_trait: protective, maternal, cunning, defiant of patriarchal tyranny
nodes.significant_event: saved her youngest son Zeus from being swallowed by Cronus by substituting a stone wrapped in swaddling clothes, hid Zeus in a cave in Crete
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughter of Uranus and Gaia, one of the twelve Titans
nodes.symbolism: the mother who defies the devouring father to preserve the next generation, the Greek parallel to the Anatolian Cybele, the mother of the gods
nodes.neumann_archetype: the Mother of the Gods, the Great Mother who rescues the divine child from the devouring father, Greek parallel to Cybele

nodes.name: Nemesis
nodes.domain: retribution, divine justice, balance, vengeance against hubris
nodes.object: scales, wheel, sword, measuring rod, bridle
nodes.physical_characteristics: winged goddess, stern and beautiful, sometimes veiled, carrying a wheel or scales
nodes.significant_event: pursued by Zeus in many forms until she became a goose and laid the egg from which Helen of Troy was born, worshipped at Rhamnus with an important cult statue
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughter of Nyx in most traditions, or of Oceanus, or of Zeus and Necessity
nodes.symbolism: the cosmic force that restores balance, divine punishment of human arrogance, the inescapability of justice, the wheel of fortune
nodes.neumann_archetype: the retributive aspect of the Great Goddess who maintains cosmic balance, ensuring that excessive pride is punished

nodes.name: Morrigan
nodes.symbolism: Celtic Terrible Mother/war goddess
nodes.neumann_archetype: Celtic war/death goddess representing the Terrible Mother.

nodes.name: Cihuacoatl
nodes.significant_event: Aztec serpent woman/earth goddess
nodes.symbolism: Mexican serpent woman; earth goddess; Terrible Mother
nodes.neumann_archetype: Mexican serpent woman representing the earth goddess.

nodes.name: Holda
nodes.domain: winter, spinning, domestic arts, the Wild Hunt, fertility, death
nodes.physical_characteristics: beautiful white-robed woman, sometimes appears as old hag, long flowing hair
nodes.significant_event: leads the Wild Hunt across the winter sky, rewards diligent spinners and punishes lazy ones, shakes her feather bed to make snow fall
nodes.birth_circumstances: pre-Christian Germanic deity surviving in folklore
nodes.symbolism: duality of nurturing and terrifying aspects of nature, winter and renewal, domestic industry as sacred feminine work
nodes.neumann_archetype: Great Mother in her dual benevolent-terrible aspect, combining nourishment with death

nodes.name: Groa
nodes.significant_event: Sings magic songs over Thor
nodes.symbolism: Seeress who heals with magic songs; feminine wisdom figure
nodes.neumann_archetype: Sings magic songs over Thor. Feminine wisdom/seeress tradition.

nodes.name: Europa
nodes.character_trait: beautiful, innocent, chosen by the gods
nodes.significant_event: abducted by Zeus in the form of a white bull who carried her across the sea to Crete, where she bore him Minos, Rhadamanthys, and Sarpedon
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughter of the Phoenician king Agenor and queen Telephassa
nodes.symbolism: the maiden seized by divine power in bull form, the transfer of civilization from East to West, the bull as symbol of the Great Goddess appropriated by the sky god
nodes.neumann_archetype: the maiden figure connected to bull symbolism of the Great Goddess, the feminine carried away by the masculine divine

nodes.name: Pandora
nodes.domain: creation, womankind, curiosity, all gifts, deception
nodes.physical_characteristics: beautiful woman fashioned from clay by Hephaestus, adorned by all the gods
nodes.significant_event: opened the jar releasing all evils into the world, only Hope remained inside, sent by Zeus as a punishment disguised as a gift to Epimetheus
nodes.birth_circumstances: molded from earth by Hephaestus on Zeus orders as punishment for Prometheus theft of fire, each god gave her a gift
nodes.symbolism: the all-giver whose gifts include suffering, the feminine as both blessing and curse in patriarchal mythology, curiosity as the price of knowledge
nodes.neumann_archetype: the all-giver aspect of the feminine, associated with Aphrodite as the vessel containing both beauty and destruction

nodes.name: Aruru
nodes.significant_event: Creatress/potter figure; variant of Mama/Nintu
nodes.symbolism: Creatress as potter; creates humanity from clay
nodes.neumann_archetype: Creatress/potter figure. Variant of Mama/Nintu.

nodes.name: Mama
nodes.significant_event: 'Mama recited the incantation'; wise creatress with Ea
nodes.symbolism: Wise creatress; recites incantations of creation; variant of Aruru/Nintu
nodes.neumann_archetype: Wise creatress. 'Mama recited the incantation; when she completed...'

nodes.name: Siren
nodes.domain: death, enchantment, the sea, music, temptation
nodes.physical_characteristics: part woman part bird, or beautiful women on a rocky shore, singing with irresistible voices
nodes.significant_event: lured sailors to their deaths with their irresistible singing, Odysseus survived by having himself bound to the mast while his crew plugged their ears, the Argonauts survived through Orpheus outsinging them
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughters of the river god Achelous and one of the Muses, or of Phorcys
nodes.symbolism: the deadly allure of forbidden knowledge, enchantment as the dissolution of the conscious will, the sea as the unconscious that draws consciousness to its destruction
nodes.neumann_archetype: attributes of the Archetypal Feminine as siren, the enchantment that dissolves masculine consciousness, the death enchantment of the negative feminine pole

nodes.name: Alpheus
nodes.significant_event: pursued the nymph Arethusa who fled across the sea to Sicily where she became a spring, Alpheus followed her as an underground river emerging beside her
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of the Titans Oceanus and Tethys, or of Helios
nodes.death_circumstances: Through him, Alpheus was the grandfather of Diocles, and great-grandfather of a pair of soldiers, Crethon and Orsilochus, who were slain by Aeneas during the Trojan War.
nodes.symbolism: the relentless flow of desire, the river as metaphor for pursuit across the world, unrequited love that transcends geography
nodes.neumann_archetype: the masculine principle pursuing the elusive feminine across the boundaries of land and sea

nodes.name: Aristaeus
nodes.domain: beekeeping, cheese-making, herding, olive cultivation, hunting
nodes.physical_characteristics: rustic god sometimes depicted as a winged young man
nodes.significant_event: taught humanity beekeeping, cheese-making, and olive cultivation, pursued Eurydice leading to her death by snakebite, lost his bees as divine punishment and learned the Bugonia (ox-born bees) ritual to restore them
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of Apollo and the huntress nymph Cyrene, raised by the Muses who taught him healing and prophecy
nodes.symbolism: the civilizing arts of pastoral life, the unintended consequences of desire, the death and regeneration of the bee colony as a mystery of nature
nodes.neumann_archetype: the culture hero who brings the pastoral arts to humanity, the positive masculine principle in harmony with nature

nodes.name: Asclepius
nodes.character_trait: wise, healing, compassionate, transgressive in resurrecting the dead
nodes.physical_characteristics: bearded, dignified, carrying the serpent-entwined staff of healing
nodes.significant_event: became so skilled in healing he could raise the dead, struck down by Zeus thunderbolt for upsetting the natural order, after death honored as a god with major temples at Epidaurus and Cos
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of Apollo and the mortal Coronis, cut from his dying mothers womb by Apollo, raised by the centaur Chiron who taught him the art of medicine
nodes.death_circumstances: Coronis was killed by Artemis for being unfaithful to Apollo and was laid out on a funeral pyre to be consumed, but Apollo rescued the child by cutting him from Coronis's womb.
nodes.symbolism: healing as divine art, the serpent as symbol of renewal and regeneration, the boundary between life and death that medicine transgresses
nodes.neumann_archetype: the healing son of the solar god, wielding the snake-entwined staff that connects the worlds of life and death

nodes.name: Apis
nodes.animals: serpent, bull, vulture, scarab, cow, cerberus
nodes.physical_characteristics: mythological king, sometimes associated with the sacred bull
nodes.significant_event: legendary king of Argos, taught his people the art of government, killed by Aetolus in a chariot race
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of Phoroneus in Greek tradition, or associated with the Egyptian Apis bull
nodes.death_circumstances: Initially, he was assigned a significant role in her worship, being sacrificed and reborn.
nodes.symbolism: the sacred king connected to both Greek and Egyptian royal traditions, the bull as symbol of sovereignty
nodes.neumann_archetype: the sacred king archetype, the ruler whose sovereignty is connected to the divine bull

nodes.name: Anytos
nodes.physical_characteristics: Titan or giant in Arcadian tradition, depicted in armor at Lycosura
nodes.significant_event: raised the goddess Despoina on behalf of Demeter, his statue stood alongside Despoinas at the temple of Lycosura wearing armor
nodes.birth_circumstances: one of the Titans in Arcadian tradition
nodes.symbolism: the chthonic guardian who raises the divine child, the protective masculine within the Great Mothers mysteries
nodes.neumann_archetype: the nurturing Titan who serves the Great Mother by protecting her hidden daughter

nodes.name: Agathos Daimon
nodes.domain: good fortune, vineyards, grain, household protection
nodes.physical_characteristics: serpent form or young man with cornucopia, associated with household shrines
nodes.significant_event: received a libation of unmixed wine at the end of every meal in Athenian households, closely associated with the Agathe Tyche (Good Fortune)
nodes.symbolism: the beneficent spirit protecting the household and harvest, the serpent as guardian of prosperity
nodes.neumann_archetype: the positive masculine spirit of fortune and protection at the domestic level

nodes.name: Aether
nodes.physical_characteristics: personification of the bright upper atmosphere above the clouds
nodes.significant_event: represents the pure upper air breathed by the gods, distinct from the lower air breathed by mortals
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of Erebus (Darkness) and Nyx (Night), brother of Hemera (Day)
nodes.symbolism: the divine atmosphere separating heavens from earth, the bright sky as the realm of the gods, the light that emerges from primordial darkness
nodes.neumann_archetype: the luminous masculine principle emerging from the primordial darkness of the uroboric parents

nodes.name: Agon
nodes.physical_characteristics: personification of athletic and martial competition
nodes.significant_event: had a statue at Olympia depicting the moment of contest
nodes.symbolism: the sacred nature of competition in Greek culture, struggle as a path to excellence
nodes.neumann_archetype: the masculine drive toward self-testing and triumph through struggle

nodes.name: Aion
nodes.domain: eternity, cyclical time, the ages, the zodiac
nodes.physical_characteristics: lion-headed figure entwined by a serpent, standing within a zodiac wheel, or youthful naked figure
nodes.significant_event: depicted in Mithraic mysteries as the leontocephaline figure, representing the eternal cycle of ages
nodes.birth_circumstances: primordial or orphic deity representing unbounded time
nodes.symbolism: eternity as distinct from chronological time, the cycles of cosmic ages, the zodiac as the wheel of eternal return
nodes.neumann_archetype: the uroboric eternal return, time transcending the linear into the cyclical and eternal

nodes.name: Anemoi
nodes.domain: winds, seasons, weather, the four directions
nodes.physical_characteristics: four winged and bearded gods, sometimes depicted as horse-headed, blowing from the four cardinal directions
nodes.significant_event: Boreas abducted the Athenian princess Oreithyia, Zephyrus caused the death of Hyacinthus, together they aided the Greeks at Salamis
nodes.birth_circumstances: sons of Eos (Dawn) and Astraeus (Stars): Boreas (North), Notus (South), Eurus (East), and Zephyrus (West)
nodes.symbolism: the four directions as elemental forces, wind as the breath of the cosmos, the power and danger of the elements
nodes.neumann_archetype: the masculine elemental forces that both destroy and invigorate, the breath of the cosmic order

nodes.name: Agreus and Nomios
nodes.physical_characteristics: son of Hermes, combining hunter and herdsman
nodes.significant_event: Agreus inherited the gift of prophecy from his mother Sose and was a skilled hunter, Nomios was a shepherd god
nodes.symbolism: the dual mastery of hunting and herding as complementary aspects of pastoral civilization
nodes.neumann_archetype: the dual pastoral hero combining the active (hunter) and contemplative (herder) masculine

nodes.name: Acratopotes
nodes.physical_characteristics: daimon of unmixed wine, associated with drunkenness
nodes.significant_event: worshipped in the district of Munychia in Athens where a statue depicted him
nodes.symbolism: uninhibited drinking, the wildness of wine without the civilizing dilution with water
nodes.neumann_archetype: the shadow aspect of Dionysiac worship, intoxication without moderation

nodes.name: Aegipan
nodes.physical_characteristics: sea-goat with the upper body of a goat and lower body of a fish
nodes.significant_event: helped Zeus in the battle against the Titans by blowing a conch shell to create panic, or helped recover Zeus sinews stolen by Typhon, honored as the constellation Capricornus
nodes.birth_circumstances: According to Hyginus, Aegipan was the son of Zeus (some sources say his son Apollo) and Aega (also named Boetis or Aix), and was transferred to the stars.
nodes.symbolism: divine aid from the wild places, panic as a weapon of the gods, the goat-fish hybrid representing the boundary between land and sea
nodes.neumann_archetype: the wild nature spirit who assists the sky father in his battle against the primordial chaos

nodes.name: Aeolus
nodes.character_trait: hospitable, obedient to the gods, sovereign over winds
nodes.physical_characteristics: king dwelling on the floating island of Aeolia
nodes.significant_event: gave Odysseus a bag containing all adverse winds to ensure safe passage home, but his crew opened it and they were blown back
nodes.birth_circumstances: In Greek mythology, Aeolus (; , ), the son of Hippotes, was the ruler of the winds encountered by Odysseus in Homer's Odyssey.
nodes.symbolism: divine control over natural forces, the fragility of human discipline before temptation
nodes.neumann_archetype: the keeper of elemental forces, the threshold guardian on the heros journey

nodes.name: Aoös
nodes.significant_event: personification of the river Aoos in Thessaly
nodes.birth_circumstances: Aoös (Greek Αώος, pronounced aO-os) was another name for god Adonis and also the mythic son of Eos and Cephalus who became the first king of Cyprus.
nodes.symbolism: the living waters of northern Greece, the river as divine being
nodes.neumann_archetype: the masculine water principle of the specific regional landscape

nodes.name: Acmon
nodes.physical_characteristics: primordial being sometimes identified with Uranus
nodes.significant_event: in some traditions identified with Uranus himself as the vault of heaven conceived as a great anvil
nodes.birth_circumstances: In another genealogy, incorrectly attributed to Hesiod, Acmon is the son of Gaia, and in some sources he is identified with Uranus himself.
nodes.symbolism: the sky as anvil upon which the cosmos is forged, the connection between heavenly and smithing imagery
nodes.neumann_archetype: the primordial sky conceived as the workspace of cosmic creation

nodes.name: Atlas
nodes.character_trait: enduring, knowledgeable, burdened, wise in astronomy
nodes.physical_characteristics: enormous Titan bearing the heavens on his shoulders, straining under the cosmic weight
nodes.significant_event: condemned by Zeus to hold up the sky after the Titans defeat in the Titanomachy, tricked by Heracles during the quest for the golden apples of the Hesperides, turned to stone by Perseus using Medusas head
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of the Titan Iapetus and the Oceanid Asia or Clymene, brother of Prometheus, Epimetheus, and Menoetius
nodes.symbolism: the burden of cosmic knowledge, the weight of holding the world together, endurance under impossible obligation
nodes.neumann_archetype: the Titan who bears the weight of the separation between heaven and earth, embodying the burden of cosmic consciousness

nodes.name: Castor and Pollux
nodes.physical_characteristics: twin young men, often helmeted and mounted, associated with twin stars
nodes.significant_event: Pollux shared his immortality with his dead twin Castor so they alternate between Olympus and Hades, they became the constellation Gemini, patrons of sailors who appear as St Elmos fire
nodes.birth_circumstances: sons of Leda, Castor was mortal son of Tyndareus while Pollux was divine son of Zeus who came to Leda as a swan, born from an egg
nodes.symbolism: the bond of brotherhood that transcends death, the Indo-European Divine Twins archetype, mortality and immortality as twin aspects of human nature
nodes.neumann_archetype: the Divine Twins representing the duality of mortal and immortal, the dual hero who bridges the worlds

nodes.name: Smicrus
nodes.significant_event: worshipped in local hero cult in Crete
nodes.birth_circumstances: Smicrus was either the son of Democlus, a man from Delphi, or an unnamed man from the island of Ceos.
nodes.symbolism: the local hero tradition of Crete
nodes.neumann_archetype: the local hero archetype in Cretan tradition

nodes.name: DionysusBacchus
nodes.domain: wine, ecstasy, mystery religion, fertility, death and rebirth, orphic mysteries
nodes.object: thyrsus, grapevine, ivy crown, mirror, kantharos, mask
nodes.animals: bull, panther, tiger, serpent, leopard, goat, dolphin, donkey
nodes.character_trait: ecstatic, wild, liberating, maddening, twice-born, dismembered and reborn
nodes.physical_characteristics: bull-horned, sometimes serpentine, youthful or bearded, crowned with ivy
nodes.significant_event: as Zagreus was dismembered by the Titans who were then struck by Zeus thunderbolt, humanity arose from their ashes containing both Titanic and Dionysiac elements
nodes.birth_circumstances: in Orphic tradition son of Zeus and Persephone as Zagreus, torn apart by Titans and reborn through Zeus thigh, the twice-born god
nodes.symbolism: the divine spark within mortal flesh, dismemberment and reassembly as the mystery of death and rebirth, the Orphic doctrine of the souls divine origin and bodily imprisonment
nodes.neumann_archetype: the dying and rising god of the mystery tradition, the son-lover of the Great Mother who is dismembered and reborn, representing the transformation of consciousness

nodes.name: Astraeus
nodes.physical_characteristics: Titan of the dusk, father of the stars and winds
nodes.significant_event: married the dawn goddess Eos and fathered the four Winds (Boreas, Notus, Euros, Zephyrus) and the five Wandering Stars (planets)
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of the Titans Crius and Eurybia
nodes.symbolism: the dusk that gives birth to the stars, the union of twilight and dawn producing all celestial phenomena
nodes.neumann_archetype: the masculine twilight principle whose union with the feminine dawn generates the visible cosmos

nodes.name: Caerus
nodes.domain: opportunity, the fleeting moment, luck, kairos
nodes.character_trait: fleeting, beautiful, elusive, bald at the back
nodes.physical_characteristics: beautiful youth with long forelock but bald at the back of the head, standing on a razor or winged ball
nodes.significant_event: worshipped at Olympia where a famous statue by Lysippos depicted him, the forelock must be seized as he passes or the opportunity is lost forever
nodes.birth_circumstances: youngest son of Zeus
nodes.symbolism: the critical moment that can only be seized from the front, opportunity that once passed cannot be recalled, time as quality not quantity
nodes.neumann_archetype: the masculine moment of decisive consciousness, the instant of transformation that must be grasped

nodes.name: Chronos
nodes.physical_characteristics: aged figure with grey beard, sometimes serpentine, distinct from Cronus the Titan
nodes.significant_event: in Orphic cosmogony, entwines with Ananke around the cosmic egg, from which Phanes the first god is born
nodes.birth_circumstances: self-generated primordial being in Orphic tradition, or equated with Cronus
nodes.symbolism: time as the all-consuming force, the eternal cycle that creates and destroys, distinct from Cronus though often confused with him
nodes.neumann_archetype: the uroboric serpent of time encircling creation, the masculine counterpart to Necessity

nodes.name: Coeus
nodes.domain: intellect, the axis of heaven, inquiry
nodes.physical_characteristics: Titan associated with the celestial axis, the pole of heaven around which the stars revolve
nodes.significant_event: married his sister Phoebe and fathered Leto and Asteria, imprisoned in Tartarus after the Titanomachy
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of Uranus and Gaia, one of the twelve Titans
nodes.symbolism: the cosmic intellect, the axis around which celestial knowledge revolves, the questioning mind
nodes.neumann_archetype: the masculine intellectual principle among the Titans, the axis of heavenly consciousness

nodes.name: Crius
nodes.physical_characteristics: one of the elder Titans, sometimes associated with the constellation Aries
nodes.significant_event: married Eurybia and fathered Astraeus, Pallas, and Perses, imprisoned in Tartarus after the Titanomachy
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of Uranus and Gaia, one of the twelve Titans
nodes.symbolism: the ordering of the heavens into constellations, the ram as celestial symbol
nodes.neumann_archetype: the Titan principle of celestial structure, the masculine ordering of the night sky

nodes.name: Deimos
nodes.physical_characteristics: personification of dread and terror on the battlefield
nodes.significant_event: accompanies his father Ares on the battlefield spreading terror among warriors, depicted on Agamemnons shield alongside Phobos and the Gorgoneion
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of Ares and Aphrodite, brother of Phobos (Fear)
nodes.symbolism: the psychological weapon of terror in war, dread as the child of violence and desire, the paralysis of fear before battle
nodes.neumann_archetype: the shadow offspring of the war god, the masculine principle of terror that dissolves consciousness in battle

nodes.name: Enyalius
nodes.physical_characteristics: war god, sometimes depicted fully armed
nodes.significant_event: worshipped with war dances by Spartan youths before battle, young Spartans sacrificed puppies to him
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of Ares and Enyo, or son of Cronus and Rhea, or an epithet of Ares himself
nodes.symbolism: the fury of battle as a divine force, war as a sacred masculine domain, the battle frenzy that seizes warriors
nodes.neumann_archetype: the shadow of the war god, the undifferentiated masculine fury of combat

nodes.name: Dactyls
nodes.physical_characteristics: small finger-sized beings associated with the forge and mountains
nodes.significant_event: discovered iron-working and metallurgy on Mount Ida, invented rhythm and musical measures, associated with the Mysteries of Samothrace
nodes.birth_circumstances: born from the earth of Mount Ida when Rhea (or Cybele) pressed her fingers into the soil during the birth pangs of Zeus
nodes.symbolism: the magical origin of metalworking, the creative fingers of the earth mother, craft as a divine mystery
nodes.neumann_archetype: the creative dwarfs born from the Great Mothers labor, the miniature masculine as the agent of transformative craft

nodes.name: Comus
nodes.physical_characteristics: winged youth carrying a torch and wearing a wreath of flowers, sometimes depicted drowsy with wine
nodes.significant_event: presides over nighttime festivals and revels, the patron of merry-making that follows banquets
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of Dionysus and Circe in some traditions
nodes.symbolism: the joy of nocturnal celebration, festivity as a sacred release, the divine permission to revel
nodes.neumann_archetype: the Dionysiac masculine in its lightest and most playful aspect, revelry as a path to joy

nodes.name: Darrhon
nodes.physical_characteristics: Macedonian healing god, depicted on horseback in some representations
nodes.significant_event: worshipped as a healing deity in Macedonia, later syncretized with Asclepius in Hellenistic times
nodes.symbolism: the warrior who heals, the Macedonian tradition of the mounted healer-protector
nodes.neumann_archetype: the masculine healing archetype combined with the warrior, the horseman-healer of northern Greece

nodes.name: Epactaeus
nodes.physical_characteristics: god of the shore and coastline
nodes.significant_event: worshipped by coastal communities as a protector of the shoreline
nodes.symbolism: the divine protection of the liminal zone between land and sea
nodes.neumann_archetype: the masculine guardian of the boundary between earth and water

nodes.name: Cronus
nodes.domain: time, harvest, sovereignty, the Golden Age
nodes.character_trait: cunning, tyrannical, devouring, fearful of prophecy
nodes.physical_characteristics: bearded elder, wielding the sickle with which he castrated his father
nodes.significant_event: castrated his father Uranus with a sickle at his mothers urging, swallowed each of his children at birth to prevent a prophecy of his overthrow, defeated by Zeus in the Titanomachy and imprisoned in Tartarus
nodes.birth_circumstances: youngest of the twelve Titans, son of Uranus and Gaia
nodes.symbolism: the devouring father who consumes his own progeny, the Golden Age ruler overthrown by the new order, time that consumes all things
nodes.neumann_archetype: the devouring father archetype, the Terrible Father who must be overthrown by the hero-son for consciousness to emerge

nodes.name: Eleos
nodes.physical_characteristics: gentle goddess worshipped with an altar in the Athenian agora
nodes.significant_event: had an altar in the Athenian agora where those seeking mercy could take refuge, uniquely among Greek deities she received no sacrifice but only tears and entreaties
nodes.symbolism: mercy as a civic virtue, compassion as divine rather than weakness, the altar of pity as the heart of democratic Athens
nodes.neumann_archetype: the positive feminine as compassion, the mercy that tempers the severity of justice

nodes.name: Epiales
nodes.physical_characteristics: nightmare spirit that sits on the sleepers chest
nodes.significant_event: causes nightmares by pressing on sleepers chests, the experience of sleep paralysis personified
nodes.birth_circumstances: born from Nyx in some traditions
nodes.symbolism: the terror that comes in sleep, the nightmare as a visitation by a malevolent spirit, the weight of unconscious fear
nodes.neumann_archetype: the shadow incubus of the unconscious, the terrifying visitor from the depths of sleep

nodes.name: Corus
nodes.domain: surfeit, satiety, excess, arrogance born of plenty
nodes.physical_characteristics: spirit of insolent excess born from too much prosperity
nodes.significant_event: associated with the moral sequence: prosperity leads to koros (surfeit), surfeit leads to hybris (arrogance), hybris leads to ate (ruin)
nodes.birth_circumstances: child of Hybris (Hubris) in some accounts
nodes.symbolism: the dangerous excess of prosperity that breeds arrogance, the fatal sequence from wealth to downfall
nodes.neumann_archetype: the inflation of consciousness from too much abundance, the psychic excess that precedes the fall

nodes.name: Chrysus
nodes.significant_event: personification of gold as a divine substance, associated with the corrupting power of wealth in moral tales
nodes.symbolism: gold as both the noblest metal and the most corrupting, the divine shine that attracts and destroys
nodes.neumann_archetype: the luminous shadow of consciousness, the golden allure of the material world

nodes.name: Elasioi
nodes.physical_characteristics: spirits who drive away disease and evil
nodes.significant_event: invoked in ritual to ward off plague and pestilence, associated with Apollo in his healing aspect
nodes.birth_circumstances: Either way, the Elasioi were said to be children or descendants of the heroine Alexida, daughter of the deified Amphiaraus.
nodes.symbolism: the divine forces that drive away affliction, propitiation as a communal healing act
nodes.neumann_archetype: the protective spirits that guard the boundary between health and disease

nodes.name: Hypnos
nodes.object: poppy, horn of sleep-inducing opium, branch dripping Lethe water
nodes.character_trait: gentle, irresistible, all-subduing, twin of death
nodes.physical_characteristics: winged youth, or winged old man, gentle and soft, dwelling in a cave of eternal twilight
nodes.significant_event: put Zeus to sleep at Heras request so she could work against the Trojans, fled to Nyx when Zeus woke and raged, Zeus dared not pursue because even he feared Nyx
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of Nyx, twin brother of Thanatos (Death)
nodes.symbolism: sleep as the gentle twin of death, the dissolution of consciousness each night, the cave of twilight between waking and the underworld
nodes.neumann_archetype: the dissolution of ego-consciousness, the nightly return to the uroboric state of undifferentiation

nodes.name: Homer
nodes.domain: epic poetry, bardic tradition, memory, the Muses
nodes.character_trait: blind, inspired, all-seeing through inner vision, master poet
nodes.physical_characteristics: traditionally depicted as a blind old man with a staff, the supreme bard
nodes.significant_event: composed the Iliad and Odyssey, the foundational texts of Western literature, said to have competed with Hesiod in a poetry contest
nodes.birth_circumstances: traditionally born in Ionia, son of various fathers in different traditions, divinely inspired by the Muses
nodes.symbolism: blindness as inner sight, the poet as the vessel of divine memory, the oral tradition as the foundation of civilization, the Muses speaking through a mortal voice
nodes.neumann_archetype: the blind seer-poet who channels the Great Mothers memory (Mnemosyne) through masculine creative voice, the archetypal vessel of cultural consciousness

nodes.name: Heracles
nodes.object: club, lion skin, bow, golden apples
nodes.animals: eagle, serpent, snake, bull, horse, lion, ram, boar, dog, dragon, centaur, minotaur, hydra, cerberus
nodes.character_trait: strong, enduring, wrathful, gluttonous, courageous, suffering
nodes.physical_characteristics: massively muscular, bearded, wearing lion skin, carrying club
nodes.significant_event: completed the Twelve Labors imposed by King Eurystheus, killed his own children in a fit of madness sent by Hera, freed Prometheus, died on a funeral pyre and was apotheosized to Olympus
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of Zeus and the mortal Alcmene, conceived when Zeus took the form of her husband Amphitryon
nodes.symbolism: the mortal who achieves divinity through suffering and labor, civilization triumphing over the monstrous, the hero who must endure the Great Mothers persecution to achieve immortality
nodes.neumann_archetype: the supreme hero who overcomes the Terrible Mother in all her forms through the twelve labors, achieving transformation from mortal to divine

nodes.name: Hephaestus
nodes.domain: fire, metalworking, craftsmanship, forging, volcanoes, sculpture
nodes.character_trait: creative, industrious, patient, bitter, cunning, skilled
nodes.physical_characteristics: lame, bearded, muscular arms and chest, deformed feet, sooty from the forge
nodes.significant_event: forged the weapons and armor of the gods, created Pandora from clay, trapped Ares and Aphrodite in an unbreakable net, built automatons and mechanical servants
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of Hera alone without a father, or son of Zeus and Hera, cast from Olympus as an infant because of his lameness
nodes.symbolism: the creative power born from rejection, the transformative fire that shapes civilization, the artisan god whose physical imperfection produces perfect works
nodes.neumann_archetype: the rejected son of the Great Mother who transforms his suffering into creative mastery over fire and metal

nodes.name: Helios
nodes.object: sun chariot, golden cup, aureole, crown of rays
nodes.physical_characteristics: radiant, beardless or bearded, crowned with rays of light, driving a golden chariot across the sky
nodes.significant_event: drives the sun chariot daily across the sky from east to west, told Demeter what happened to Persephone, his son Phaethon lost control of the chariot and nearly burned the earth
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of the Titans Hyperion and Theia, brother of Selene and Eos
nodes.symbolism: the all-seeing eye of heaven, the regularity of cosmic order, the danger of mortal presumption in wielding divine power
nodes.neumann_archetype: the solar consciousness that illuminates all things, the all-seeing witness of the cosmos

nodes.name: Iacchus
nodes.domain: the Eleusinian Mysteries, procession, ecstasy, wine
nodes.physical_characteristics: beautiful youth carrying a torch, leading the mystai in procession
nodes.significant_event: led the sacred procession from Athens to Eleusis on the sixth day of the Mysteries, his name was shouted in the ritual cry Iacche
nodes.birth_circumstances: variously identified as the son of Demeter, son of Persephone, or an aspect of Dionysus
nodes.symbolism: the ecstatic leader of the mystery procession, the torchlight that guides initiates through the darkness toward revelation, the Dionysiac element within the Eleusinian Mysteries
nodes.neumann_archetype: the divine child as the guide through the mystery, the youthful masculine light that leads consciousness through the transformative darkness of the Great Mothers rites

nodes.name: Harpocrates
nodes.physical_characteristics: young child with finger raised to his lips in a gesture of silence
nodes.significant_event: became widely worshipped in the Greco-Roman world as the god of silence and secrecy, associated with mystery cults
nodes.birth_circumstances: Greek adaptation of the Egyptian child-god Horus (Har-pa-khered, Horus the Child), reinterpreted as a god of silence
nodes.symbolism: the sacred silence of mystery traditions, secrecy as a divine quality, the child-god who knows but does not speak
nodes.neumann_archetype: the divine child in his silent aspect, consciousness that contains truth but does not articulate it

nodes.name: Geras
nodes.domain: old age, decay, the final stage of life
nodes.physical_characteristics: tiny shriveled old figure, depicted on Greek vases as a small wrinkled man confronted by Heracles
nodes.significant_event: depicted in vase paintings being confronted or defeated by Heracles, symbolizing the heros desire to overcome aging
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of Nyx alone, or of Nyx and Erebus
nodes.death_circumstances: Geras as embodied in humans represented a virtue: the more gēras a man acquired, the more kleos (fame) and arete (excellence and courage) he was considered to have.
nodes.symbolism: the inevitability of decay, old age as a cosmic force, the enemy that not even heroes can truly defeat
nodes.neumann_archetype: the devouring aspect of time, the withering of the masculine hero-consciousness

nodes.name: Iapetus
nodes.physical_characteristics: Titan ancestor of the human race through his sons
nodes.significant_event: fathered Atlas, Prometheus, Epimetheus, and Menoetius, whose actions shaped the relationship between gods and humanity, imprisoned in Tartarus after the Titanomachy
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of Uranus and Gaia, one of the twelve Titans
nodes.symbolism: the Titan whose lineage defines the human condition: foresight (Prometheus), hindsight (Epimetheus), endurance (Atlas), and recklessness (Menoetius)
nodes.neumann_archetype: the ancestral Titan whose sons embody the cardinal qualities of human consciousness

nodes.name: Epimetheus
nodes.significant_event: despite Prometheus warning he accepted Pandora as a gift from Zeus, opening the way for all evils to enter the world, distributed all animal traits but left nothing for humanity
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of the Titan Iapetus and the Oceanid Clymene, brother of Prometheus, Atlas, and Menoetius
nodes.symbolism: the folly of acting without foresight, hindsight as the complement to forethought, the acceptance of dangerous gifts
nodes.neumann_archetype: the shadow of the culture hero, the brother who lacks consciousness and thereby brings catastrophe

nodes.name: Hyperion
nodes.physical_characteristics: the Titan who goes above, embodiment of heavenly light
nodes.significant_event: married his sister Theia and fathered Helios (Sun), Selene (Moon), and Eos (Dawn), the three luminaries of the sky
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of Uranus and Gaia, one of the twelve Titans
nodes.symbolism: the primordial light that precedes and generates the visible celestial bodies, the watcher from above
nodes.neumann_archetype: the primordial solar masculine, the light-consciousness that precedes the differentiated sun

nodes.name: Hesperus
nodes.domain: the evening star, Venus at dusk, twilight
nodes.physical_characteristics: handsome youth carrying a torch, the evening star personified
nodes.significant_event: identified with the planet Venus as it appears at dusk, in later tradition reunited with his brother Eosphorus when they were recognized as the same planet
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of Eos (Dawn) and Cephalus, or of Atlas, brother of Eosphorus (the morning star)
nodes.symbolism: the star that heralds the night, beauty at the threshold of darkness, the luminous guide into evening
nodes.neumann_archetype: the masculine light-bearer who guides consciousness toward the night, the twilight animus

nodes.name: Epiphron
nodes.physical_characteristics: spirit of prudence and careful thought
nodes.significant_event: embodies the virtue of thinking before acting, the opposite of recklessness
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of Erebus and Nyx in some traditions
nodes.symbolism: the virtue of careful consideration, prudence as a divine quality, the thoughtfulness that prevents disaster
nodes.neumann_archetype: the cautious aspect of consciousness, the reflective principle before action

nodes.name: Gelos
nodes.significant_event: Plutarch mentions him as a companion at parties, part of the retinue of Dionysus
nodes.birth_circumstances: a daimon or minor deity personifying laughter
nodes.symbolism: laughter as a divine gift, the comic spirit as a balancing force against tragedy
nodes.neumann_archetype: the positive shadow of consciousness, the laughter that liberates from the weight of seriousness

nodes.name: Epidotes
nodes.domain: abundance, bounty, he who gives increase
nodes.significant_event: an epithet of Dionysus or a separate benevolent spirit who grants increase to crops and herds
nodes.symbolism: the divine power of increase in agriculture and animal husbandry, bounty as a gift of the gods
nodes.neumann_archetype: the positive masculine as the giver of increase, the bountiful aspect of the vegetation god

nodes.name: Horkos
nodes.physical_characteristics: spirit of the oath who punishes those who break their sworn word
nodes.significant_event: pursues and punishes all who break oaths, the most feared of the children of Strife because his punishment is inescapable
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of Eris (Strife) according to Hesiod
nodes.symbolism: the sacred binding power of the oath, the terrible consequences of breaking ones word, the divine enforcement of verbal contracts
nodes.neumann_archetype: the shadow of consciousness that binds through language, the word made punishing law

nodes.name: Homados
nodes.domain: battle noise, tumult, the din of war
nodes.physical_characteristics: spirit of the battle tumult and noise of combat
nodes.significant_event: personification of the overwhelming noise and confusion of battle, accompanies Ares and Enyo
nodes.symbolism: the chaos of combat reduced to pure sound, the din that overwhelms reason on the battlefield
nodes.neumann_archetype: the shadow of martial consciousness, the dissolution of rational thought in the cacophony of violence

nodes.name: Hecaterus
nodes.physical_characteristics: rustic deity, father of the Satyrs and wild beings
nodes.significant_event: father of the Satyrs, the Curetes, and the Oreads in some traditions
nodes.birth_circumstances: sometimes identified as a son of Hermes
nodes.symbolism: the rustic masculine principle from which the wild nature spirits spring
nodes.neumann_archetype: the primitive masculine creative force that generates the wild spirits of nature

nodes.name: Erikepaios
nodes.physical_characteristics: firstborn god of Orphic theology, often identified with Phanes or Dionysus
nodes.significant_event: in Orphic hymns he is the primordial creative force that sets the cosmos in motion, swallowed by Zeus who then contains all creation within himself
nodes.birth_circumstances: born from the Cosmic Egg in Orphic cosmogony
nodes.symbolism: the first creative impulse of the cosmos, the light-bearer who emerges from the cosmic egg, the god swallowed and reborn
nodes.neumann_archetype: the divine child as the first light of cosmic consciousness emerging from the uroboric egg

nodes.name: Melicertes
nodes.domain: the sea, harbors, protection of sailors, transformation
nodes.physical_characteristics: young sea god, often depicted riding a dolphin
nodes.significant_event: when his mother Ino went mad and jumped into the sea with him, he was transformed into the sea god Palaemon, worshipped as protector of harbors and sailors, the Isthmian Games were said to be founded in his honor
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of Ino (Leucothea) and Athamas, originally named Melicertes
nodes.symbolism: the child transformed by drowning into a marine protector, death by water as divine transformation, the harbor god born from a mothers madness
