nodes.symbolism: light born from darkness, the daily miracle of dawn as the emergence of consciousness from the unconscious, the daughter who overcomes the mother
nodes.neumann_archetype: the light-consciousness born from the darkness of the primordial mother, the daily emergence of awareness from sleep

nodes.name: Hygieia
nodes.domain: health, hygiene, cleanliness, prevention of disease
nodes.physical_characteristics: radiant young woman feeding a serpent from a patera
nodes.significant_event: worshipped alongside her father Asclepius at his healing temples, her cult emphasized prevention of illness over cure, the Hippocratic oath invokes her name
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughter of Asclepius the god of medicine, granddaughter of Apollo
nodes.symbolism: health as a positive state rather than merely absence of disease, prevention as wisdom, the serpent of renewal fed by conscious care
nodes.neumann_archetype: the positive nurturing feminine in her aspect as preserver of health and wholeness

nodes.name: Iaso
nodes.physical_characteristics: gentle goddess of healing and recovery from illness
nodes.significant_event: worshipped alongside her father and sisters at healing sanctuaries, invoked in the Hippocratic Oath
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughter of Asclepius and Epione
nodes.symbolism: the process of recovery and cure, healing as a gradual restoration rather than an instant miracle
nodes.neumann_archetype: the nurturing feminine as the restorer of health, the gentle process of cure

nodes.name: Iris
nodes.domain: rainbow, divine messages, communication between gods and mortals, the sea
nodes.object: pitcher of Styx water, caduceus, rainbow
nodes.physical_characteristics: golden-winged goddess trailing a rainbow across the sky, carrying a pitcher
nodes.significant_event: serves as messenger of the gods particularly Hera, carries water from the River Styx for divine oaths, in the Iliad she acts as messenger between gods and mortals
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughter of the sea god Thaumas and the Oceanid Electra, sister of the Harpies
nodes.symbolism: the rainbow as bridge between heaven and earth, divine communication, the faithful servant of the cosmic order
nodes.neumann_archetype: the mediating feminine that connects the divine and human realms, the rainbow bridge between consciousness and the unconscious

nodes.name: Hebe
nodes.domain: youth, rejuvenation, the prime of life, divine service
nodes.physical_characteristics: eternally youthful and beautiful, cupbearer of the gods
nodes.significant_event: served as cupbearer to the gods until replaced by Ganymede, married Heracles after his apotheosis as his divine reward, able to rejuvenate the old
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughter of Zeus and Hera, the youngest of the Olympian family
nodes.symbolism: eternal youth as divine gift, the reward awaiting the hero who achieves immortality, youth as divine service
nodes.neumann_archetype: the positive anima as the reward for the completed hero, the maiden aspect of the Great Mother bestowed upon the victorious son

nodes.name: Idyia
nodes.physical_characteristics: Oceanid nymph whose name means She Who Knows
nodes.significant_event: wife of Aeetes king of Colchis, mother of Medea the sorceress, her name meaning knowing suggests she passed her wisdom to her daughter
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughter of Oceanus and Tethys
nodes.symbolism: the oceanic wisdom that produces the sorceress, the mother of magical knowledge, the deep knowing of the sea
nodes.neumann_archetype: the oceanic Great Mother as the source of feminine magical knowledge, the wise water from which the sorceress-daughter springs

nodes.name: Horme
nodes.physical_characteristics: spirit of impulse and the drive to action
nodes.significant_event: one of the spirits that escaped Pandoras jar, representing the drive that compels action
nodes.symbolism: the inner impulse toward effort and action, the divine force that overcomes inertia
nodes.neumann_archetype: the masculine drive of consciousness toward action and achievement

nodes.name: Homonoia
nodes.physical_characteristics: personification of concord and unanimity, depicted holding a cornucopia
nodes.significant_event: worshipped as the spirit of civic unity, had altars in several Greek cities, invoked in political assemblies to ensure unanimity
nodes.birth_circumstances: Homonoia was believed to be the daughter of Soter, the saviour daimon, and Praxidike, the goddess of judicial punishment and vengeance.
nodes.symbolism: the divine gift of social harmony, the unity that makes the polis function, concord as a sacred civic virtue
nodes.neumann_archetype: the positive feminine principle of social unity, the binding force that holds the community together

nodes.name: Hysminai
nodes.physical_characteristics: spirits of battle and combat, feminine personifications of fighting
nodes.significant_event: the battles personified, they swarm across the fields of war bringing death and destruction
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughters of Eris (Strife)
nodes.symbolism: warfare as a swarming demonic force rather than a heroic endeavor, the dehumanizing chaos of mass combat
nodes.neumann_archetype: the terrible feminine of war, battle as the devouring swarm of death

nodes.name: Ioke
nodes.physical_characteristics: spirit of the battle charge and onslaught
nodes.significant_event: personification of the furious charge in battle, the moment of onslaught
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughter of Eris (Strife)
nodes.symbolism: the momentum of the charge, the irresistible forward movement of the attacking force
nodes.neumann_archetype: the aggressive feminine of battle, the forward drive of destructive energy

nodes.name: Heimarmene
nodes.domain: fate, destiny, the allotted portion, cosmic determinism
nodes.physical_characteristics: personification of destiny and the allotted share
nodes.significant_event: represents the predetermined course of events that even the gods cannot alter, distinct from the Moirai who administer fate
nodes.symbolism: the cosmic order of predetermined events, fate as an impersonal cosmic law above even the gods, the allotted share that cannot be increased or diminished
nodes.neumann_archetype: the ultimate feminine principle of determinism, the cosmic order that contains and limits even masculine consciousness

nodes.name: Hybris
nodes.domain: hubris, excessive pride, arrogance, reckless disregard
nodes.physical_characteristics: spirit of insolence and violence born from excess
nodes.significant_event: the great sin of Greek tragedy, the overreaching pride that leads to divine punishment and destruction, embodied by figures like Niobe and Ajax
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughter of Koros (Surfeit) or born from Dysnomia (Lawlessness)
nodes.symbolism: the fatal flaw of overstepping human limits, the arrogance that brings divine retribution, the inflation that precedes the fall
nodes.neumann_archetype: the inflation of consciousness that refuses to acknowledge its limitations, the psychic crime of identifying the ego with the Self

nodes.name: Gymnastica
nodes.physical_characteristics: personification of gymnastics and athletic training
nodes.significant_event: associated with the gymnasium as a central Greek social and educational institution
nodes.symbolism: the divine dimension of physical training, the gymnasium as a sacred space for human perfection
nodes.neumann_archetype: the disciplined body as a form of consciousness, physical training as a path to excellence

nodes.name: Hesperis
nodes.physical_characteristics: Hora of the evening and sunset
nodes.significant_event: presides over the hour of sunset and the transition from day to night
nodes.symbolism: the gentle closing of the day, twilight as a sacred threshold, the western gate through which the sun departs
nodes.neumann_archetype: the feminine threshold of evening, consciousness transitioning toward the night of the unconscious

nodes.name: Leto
nodes.domain: motherhood, childhood, protection of the young
nodes.physical_characteristics: beautiful Titaness, modest and veiled, devoted mother
nodes.significant_event: wandered the earth pregnant with Apollo and Artemis while persecuted by Hera, no land would receive her until the floating island of Delos agreed, punished Niobe for boasting by having her children killed
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughter of the Titans Coeus and Phoebe, sister of Asteria
nodes.symbolism: the persecuted mother who endures suffering to bring forth the divine, the wandering that precedes the birth of light (Apollo), maternal devotion against cosmic hostility
nodes.neumann_archetype: the maternal figure who must endure the Terrible Mothers persecution (Hera) to birth the solar hero (Apollo)

nodes.name: Metis
nodes.physical_characteristics: Titaness of wisdom, sometimes depicted as a thoughtful woman
nodes.significant_event: Zeus swallowed her while she was pregnant with Athena because of a prophecy that her children would be wiser than him, Athena was later born fully armed from Zeus head
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughter of Oceanus and Tethys, first wife of Zeus
nodes.symbolism: wisdom devoured and incorporated by patriarchal power, the feminine intelligence that becomes the source of the greatest goddess from within the male god
nodes.neumann_archetype: the feminine wisdom swallowed by the patriarchal consciousness, the Great Mother incorporated into the Father who then gives birth to the wisdom-goddess Athena

nodes.name: Mnemosyne
nodes.character_trait: contemplative, preserving, foundational to all art
nodes.physical_characteristics: Titaness, sometimes depicted as a mature pensive woman
nodes.significant_event: lay with Zeus for nine consecutive nights and bore the nine Muses who preside over all arts and sciences, her pool in Hades allows the dead to remember their past lives
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughter of Uranus and Gaia, one of the twelve Titans
nodes.symbolism: memory as the foundation of all culture, the Titaness whose union with the sky god produces all the arts, remembrance as the antidote to the oblivion of death
nodes.neumann_archetype: the Great Mother of the arts, memory as the feminine ground from which consciousness and culture spring

nodes.name: Muses
nodes.domain: arts, sciences, inspiration, memory, poetry, music, dance
nodes.object: lyre, scroll, stylus, mask, globe, compass
nodes.physical_characteristics: nine beautiful women, sometimes winged, each carrying her specific attribute
nodes.significant_event: defeated the Pierides in a singing contest and transformed them into magpies, inspired Homer and Hesiod, dwell on Mount Helicon and Pieria
nodes.birth_circumstances: nine daughters of Zeus and the Titaness Mnemosyne, conceived over nine consecutive nights
nodes.death_circumstances: They were considered the source of the knowledge embodied in the poetry, lyric songs, and myths that were related orally for centuries in ancient Greek culture.
nodes.symbolism: divine inspiration as the source of all art and knowledge, the nine domains of human creativity, memory as the mother of culture
nodes.neumann_archetype: the ninefold differentiation of the Great Mothers creative aspect, the feminine as the wellspring of all cultural consciousness

nodes.name: The Litae
nodes.physical_characteristics: old wrinkled women who limp along after Ate (Ruin), daughters of Zeus
nodes.significant_event: in Homers Iliad they follow Ate trying to undo the damage she causes, those who receive them well are blessed, those who reject them are cursed with Ates ruin
nodes.birth_circumstances: parents: Zeus
nodes.symbolism: the prayers that limp after ruin trying to heal its damage, the slow healing that follows swift destruction, humility and supplication as the only remedies for the damage of pride
nodes.neumann_archetype: the crippled but persistent feminine of repair, the old women of consciousness who hobble after the destruction of inflation trying to restore wholeness

nodes.name: Lampetia
nodes.physical_characteristics: radiant nymph who tends the cattle of the sun
nodes.significant_event: together with her sister Phaethusa she guarded the sacred cattle of Helios on the island of Thrinacia, warned her father when Odysseus crew slaughtered his cattle
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughter of Helios (Sun) and the nymph Neaera
nodes.symbolism: the faithful guardian of the sacred, the daughter of light who protects the solar patrimony
nodes.neumann_archetype: the luminous feminine as the faithful guardian of the solar masculines treasure

nodes.name: Machai
nodes.physical_characteristics: spirits of battle, personifications of individual combats within a larger battle
nodes.significant_event: the individual fights that make up a battle personified as swarming spirits
nodes.birth_circumstances: offspring of Eris (Strife)
nodes.symbolism: the atomization of warfare into individual combats, battle as composed of countless smaller struggles
nodes.neumann_archetype: the fragmenting aspect of the war daimons, consciousness dissolved into multiple violent encounters

nodes.name: Kakia
nodes.physical_characteristics: beautiful woman in alluring dress who promises an easy path, the embodiment of vice
nodes.significant_event: in Prodicus fable of the Choice of Heracles she appeared alongside Arete (Virtue) and offered Heracles an easy life of pleasure, which he rejected in favor of Aretes hard path of virtue
nodes.birth_circumstances: In the Gnostic tradition, Kakia is personified as the child of the first angel and Authadia with siblings Zelos (emulation), Phthonus (envy), Erinnys (fury), and Epithymia (lust).
nodes.symbolism: the seductive ease of vice contrasted with the difficult path of virtue, beauty as a mask for moral corruption
nodes.neumann_archetype: the seductive shadow feminine who offers regression to the unconscious pleasures rather than the difficult ascent of consciousness

nodes.name: Maniae
nodes.significant_event: drive mortals to insanity, associated with the Erinyes and with Dionysiac frenzy, Hera sent them against Heracles
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughters of Nyx
nodes.symbolism: madness as a divine visitation, the dissolution of rational mind as both punishment and transformation
nodes.neumann_archetype: the terrible feminine as the dissolution of consciousness, madness as the Great Mothers reclaiming of the rational ego

nodes.name: Nike
nodes.domain: victory, triumph, athletic and military success
nodes.physical_characteristics: winged woman, often depicted in flight, carrying a wreath or palm of victory
nodes.significant_event: sided with Zeus in the Titanomachy along with her siblings, became Athenas constant companion, the famous Nike of Samothrace statue commemorates a naval victory
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughter of the Titan Pallas and the Oceanid Styx, sister of Kratos, Bia, and Zelus
nodes.symbolism: the divine moment of triumph, victory as a divine gift rather than human achievement, the winged descent of success
nodes.neumann_archetype: the positive transformative feminine as the gift of victory, the divine endorsement of the heros success

nodes.name: Methe
nodes.significant_event: personification of the effects of drinking wine, companion of Dionysus
nodes.birth_circumstances: Methe was the daughter of Dionysus in some accounts.
nodes.symbolism: intoxication as a divine state, the altered consciousness that wine produces, the dangerous gift of the vine
nodes.neumann_archetype: the feminine of intoxication, the loosening of consciousness through the Dionysiac

nodes.name: Lampsace
nodes.domain: local cult, city founding, sexual virtue
nodes.physical_characteristics: maiden heroine of the city of Lampsacus
nodes.significant_event: saved the Greek hostages held by the Bebryces and was honored as the eponymous heroine of Lampsacus, or was honored for her virtue
nodes.birth_circumstances: Lampsace was the daughter of Mandron, king of the Bebryces in Pityussa (the older name for Lampsacus).
nodes.symbolism: the maiden whose virtue or bravery founds a city, the heroine as the moral foundation of the community
nodes.neumann_archetype: the positive maiden whose self-sacrifice establishes the sacred foundation of the city

nodes.name: Kourotrophos
nodes.physical_characteristics: goddess or epithet for deities who protect children
nodes.significant_event: worshipped as a protector of infants and children, an epithet applied to Artemis, Hecate, Demeter, and other goddesses in their child-protecting aspects
nodes.symbolism: the universal feminine function of protecting the young, the divine dimension of child-rearing
nodes.neumann_archetype: the Great Mother in her nurturing and protective aspect specifically toward children

nodes.name: Neaera
nodes.significant_event: bore Helios two daughters who guarded his sacred cattle on the island of Thrinacia
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughter of Helios, mother of Lampetia and Phaethusa
nodes.symbolism: the radiant mother of the solar guardians, the sun gods beloved who produces the next generation of light-bearers
nodes.neumann_archetype: the feminine radiance of the solar tradition, the mother who generates the guardians of the masculine solar patrimony

nodes.name: Mesembria
nodes.significant_event: presides over the hour of noon when the sun is at its peak
nodes.symbolism: the moment of maximum light, the zenith of consciousness and energy in the daily cycle
nodes.neumann_archetype: the feminine of maximum solar consciousness, noon as the peak of awareness

nodes.name: Musica
nodes.significant_event: presides over the hour of music
nodes.symbolism: the sacred hour devoted to musical art, harmony as a temporal experience
nodes.neumann_archetype: the feminine ordering of time through musical consciousness

nodes.name: Nymphe
nodes.physical_characteristics: Hora of the wedding and bridal beauty
nodes.significant_event: presides over the bridal hour
nodes.symbolism: the sacred moment of the wedding, the bride as the embodiment of transformation
nodes.neumann_archetype: the feminine threshold of marriage, the sacred transition from maiden to wife

nodes.name: Freyr
nodes.significant_event: However, lacking his sword, Freyr will be killed by the fire jötunn Surtr during the events of Ragnarök.
nodes.death_circumstances: However, lacking his sword, Freyr will be killed by the fire jötunn Surtr during the events of Ragnarök.

nodes.name: Pasiphaë
nodes.physical_characteristics: beautiful queen and sorceress, daughter of the sun
nodes.significant_event: cursed by Poseidon to fall in love with the Cretan Bull as punishment for Minos breaking his vow, commissioned Daedalus to build a wooden cow so she could mate with the bull, gave birth to the Minotaur
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughter of Helios the sun god and the Oceanid Perse, sister of Circe and Aeetes, aunt of Medea
nodes.death_circumstances: Minos refused to sacrifice the animal, and sacrificed another, inferior bull instead.
nodes.symbolism: the monstrous consequence of broken vows to the gods, the feminine punished through bestial desire, the solar lineage (Helios) twisted into darkness
nodes.neumann_archetype: the Great Mother in her terrible and transgressive aspect, bearing the monster that dwells at the center of the labyrinth

nodes.name: Phaethusa
nodes.physical_characteristics: luminous nymph who guards the cattle of the Sun
nodes.significant_event: together with her sister Lampetia she guarded the sacred cattle of Helios on Thrinacia, reported to her father when Odysseus crew slaughtered the cattle
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughter of Helios (Sun) and the nymph Neaera
nodes.death_circumstances: She would have also had a brother, Phaethon, who was killed by Zeus after attempting and failing to drive Helios' chariot.
nodes.symbolism: the faithful daughter of the sun who guards the sacred herd, the solar feminine as protector of the masculine patrimony
nodes.neumann_archetype: the luminous feminine guardian of the solar patrimony, the daughters of light who protect the sacred

nodes.name: Nyx
nodes.character_trait: primordial, powerful, feared even by Zeus, mysterious
nodes.physical_characteristics: dark-robed, winged, driving a chariot of darkness across the sky
nodes.significant_event: mother of a vast brood of cosmic forces including Death, Sleep, Dreams, Fate, and Strife, even Zeus feared to displease her
nodes.birth_circumstances: born from Chaos, one of the first beings to emerge at creation
nodes.symbolism: the primordial darkness from which all things emerge, the power of the unconscious that even the ruling consciousness fears
nodes.neumann_archetype: the primordial uroboric darkness preceding consciousness, the Great Mother in her most ancient nocturnal aspect

nodes.name: Pandia
nodes.physical_characteristics: goddess of the full moon, radiant maiden
nodes.significant_event: worshipped at an Athenian festival (Pandia) held at the full moon, associated with the radiance of the full moon illuminating the night
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughter of Zeus and Selene (Moon)
nodes.symbolism: the full moon as the peak of lunar power, the daughter of the moon as the embodiment of complete lunar radiance
nodes.neumann_archetype: the full moon feminine in her complete radiance, the lunar consciousness at its brightest

nodes.name: Penia
nodes.physical_characteristics: gaunt, ragged figure personifying poverty and need
nodes.significant_event: in Platos Symposium she conceives Eros by lying with Porus (Plenty) while he sleeps drunk at a feast of the gods, making Love the child of Poverty and Plenty
nodes.symbolism: need as the mother of desire, poverty as the driving force behind ingenuity and love, want as the creative principle that seeks fulfillment
nodes.neumann_archetype: the deprived feminine that generates Eros through union with the unconscious masculine (sleeping Plenty), need as the origin of longing

nodes.name: Pheme
nodes.physical_characteristics: winged goddess covered with eyes, ears, and tongues, growing larger as she travels
nodes.significant_event: spreads news and rumor throughout the world growing larger with each retelling, neither truth nor falsehood but an indiscriminate mix, announced Didos affair with Aeneas throughout Africa
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughter of Gaia (Earth) according to Virgil
nodes.symbolism: the uncontrollable nature of rumor, fame as a monster that grows with each telling, the indistinguishability of truth and falsehood in public discourse
nodes.neumann_archetype: the archetypal spread of consciousness through collective communication, the positive and negative aspects of shared knowledge

nodes.name: Oenotropae
nodes.domain: wine, olive, grain, agriculture, miraculous transformation
nodes.physical_characteristics: three sisters with the divine gift of transforming earth into food and drink
nodes.significant_event: could transform whatever they touched into grain, wine, and olive oil respectively, kidnapped by Agamemnon to supply the Greek army at Troy, freed by Dionysus who turned them into doves
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughters of King Anius of Delos, granted their powers by Dionysus
nodes.symbolism: the miraculous transformation of nature into sustenance, the three essential Greek foods as divine gifts, the daughters whose gifts are exploited by war
nodes.neumann_archetype: the triple feminine as the transformative power that turns raw nature into the three pillars of Mediterranean civilization

nodes.name: Phoebe
nodes.physical_characteristics: bright Titaness associated with the moon and prophetic light
nodes.significant_event: held the oracle at Delphi before her grandson Apollo, passed it to her daughter Themis who passed it to Apollo, establishing the prophetic succession
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughter of Uranus and Gaia, one of the twelve Titans
nodes.symbolism: the lunar light of prophecy, the feminine origin of the Delphic oracle, radiance as the prerequisite for prophetic vision
nodes.neumann_archetype: the luminous feminine Titan as the original holder of prophetic consciousness, passing it through the maternal line

nodes.name: Oizys
nodes.significant_event: the personification of woe and suffering that afflicts humanity, one of the evils from Pandoras jar
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughter of Nyx alone, or twin sister of Momus
nodes.symbolism: misery as a cosmic force, suffering as a divine affliction rather than mere accident, the weight of existence
nodes.neumann_archetype: the dark feminine of suffering, the Great Mothers withholding aspect experienced as existential pain

nodes.name: Nysiads
nodes.physical_characteristics: rain nymphs who nursed the infant Dionysus on Mount Nysa
nodes.significant_event: nursed the infant Dionysus on Mount Nysa, teaching him the secrets of wine, later placed among the stars as the Hyades
nodes.symbolism: the divine nurses who raise the wine god, the mountain as the nursery of the divine, the rain nymphs who become stars
nodes.neumann_archetype: the nurturing feminine collective that raises the divine child on the sacred mountain, the Great Mothers multiple aspects as nurses

nodes.name: Peitharchia
nodes.physical_characteristics: spirit of obedience and compliance with authority
nodes.significant_event: personification of the discipline and obedience that maintains military and civic order
nodes.symbolism: obedience as a divine virtue, the discipline that makes armies and cities function
nodes.neumann_archetype: the ordering consciousness that submits the individual will to the collective good

nodes.name: Palioxis
nodes.physical_characteristics: spirit of battlefield rout and retreat
nodes.significant_event: the spirit of flight from battle, the counter-force to Proioxis (the battle charge), accompanies Ares
nodes.symbolism: the moment when an army breaks and flees, retreat as a demonic force that seizes warriors, the dissolution of martial courage
nodes.neumann_archetype: the shadow of martial consciousness, the moment when the heros will collapses and flight takes over

nodes.name: Panacea
nodes.physical_characteristics: divine healer, one of the healing sisterhood
nodes.significant_event: invoked in the Hippocratic Oath alongside her father and sisters, represents the complete cure of all disease
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughter of Asclepius and Epione, sister of Iaso, Hygieia, Aceso, and Aegle
nodes.symbolism: the universal remedy, the dream of complete healing, medicine as a divine aspiration
nodes.neumann_archetype: the nurturing feminine in her aspect as total restoration, the ideal of perfect healing

nodes.name: Pepromene
nodes.physical_characteristics: personification of the destined portion allotted to each mortal
nodes.significant_event: related to Heimarmene and the Moirai but representing the individual allotment of fate
nodes.symbolism: the personal destiny that cannot be altered, the portion assigned before birth
nodes.neumann_archetype: the feminine principle of individual destiny, each souls allotted share of existence

nodes.name: Pasikrata
nodes.physical_characteristics: epithet of Persephone as the absolute ruler of the dead
nodes.significant_event: worshipped as Pasikrata (All-Powerful) in her aspect as the dread queen of the underworld who rules all the dead without exception
nodes.symbolism: Persephone at her most terrible, the maiden who became the absolute queen of death, the totality of underworld power
nodes.neumann_archetype: the Great Mother as absolute ruler of the realm of death, the kore transformed into the terrible queen

nodes.name: Philyra
nodes.physical_characteristics: beautiful Oceanid nymph or Titaness, sometimes depicted as half-horse
nodes.significant_event: loved by Cronus who transformed himself into a horse to mate with her, bore the centaur Chiron, later transformed into a linden tree
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughter of Oceanus, or a Thessalian nymph
nodes.symbolism: the feminine wisdom that generates the wisest of all beings (Chiron), the nymph transformed into a tree, nature as the source of healing knowledge
nodes.neumann_archetype: the wise oceanic feminine who bears the great healer-teacher (Chiron), the Great Mother as the source of all herbal and medical wisdom

nodes.name: Opora
nodes.domain: autumn, fruit harvest, abundance, late summer
nodes.physical_characteristics: goddess of the autumn fruit harvest, depicted carrying fruit
nodes.significant_event: personification of the late summer and autumn when fruits ripen, consort of Dionysus in comic poetry (Aristophanes Peace)
nodes.birth_circumstances: In ancient Greek mythology and religion, Opora () is a minor goddess connected to fruit, the harvest, especially wine harvest, and the season of autumn.
nodes.symbolism: the ripeness of autumn, the mature harvest before the descent into winter, the fullness of the agricultural year
nodes.neumann_archetype: the Great Mother in her harvest aspect, the mature feminine abundance before the dying of the year

nodes.name: Paregoros
nodes.significant_event: personification of the words and feelings that bring comfort to the grieving
nodes.symbolism: the divine gift of comfort in grief, consolation as a cosmic force, the gentle voice that soothes suffering
nodes.neumann_archetype: the positive feminine as the comforting aspect of the Great Mother, the voice that consoles consciousness in its suffering

nodes.name: Semele
nodes.domain: earth, motherhood, divine epiphany, death through divine encounter
nodes.character_trait: beautiful, mortal, trusting, doomed by divine love
nodes.physical_characteristics: beautiful Theban princess, mortal beloved of Zeus
nodes.significant_event: tricked by Hera into asking Zeus to reveal himself in his true divine form, consumed by his thunderbolt, the unborn Dionysus was rescued from her womb and sewn into Zeus thigh, later rescued from the underworld by Dionysus and made immortal as Thyone
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughter of Cadmus and Harmonia, princess of Thebes
nodes.symbolism: the mortal who is destroyed by encountering the divine directly, the mother of the god who dies to give birth, later redeemed by her own divine son
nodes.neumann_archetype: the mortal vessel of the divine child who is destroyed by the full power of the sky father, later rescued from death by the son she bore

nodes.name: Themis
nodes.domain: divine law, justice, natural order, prophecy, custom, assemblies
nodes.physical_characteristics: stately Titaness, sometimes blindfolded, holding scales of justice
nodes.significant_event: second wife of Zeus before Hera, bore the Horae (Seasons) and the Moirai (Fates), held the oracle at Delphi before Apollo, summoned the gods to assembly
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughter of Uranus and Gaia, one of the twelve Titans
nodes.death_circumstances: Dike executed the law of judgments and sentencing and, together with her mother Themis, she carried out the final decisions of Moirai.
nodes.symbolism: divine law as distinct from human legislation, the natural order that precedes and transcends mortal institutions, prophecy as the voice of cosmic justice
nodes.neumann_archetype: the ancient feminine wisdom that establishes cosmic law, the Titaness whose authority precedes and undergirds the Olympian order

nodes.name: Theia
nodes.domain: sight, light, precious metals, brilliance, the shining sky
nodes.character_trait: luminous, precious, ancient, generative of light
nodes.physical_characteristics: radiant Titaness, mother of celestial lights
nodes.significant_event: married her brother Hyperion and bore Helios (Sun), Selene (Moon), and Eos (Dawn), the three sources of earthly light
nodes.birth_circumstances: eldest daughter of Uranus (Sky) and Gaia (Earth), one of the twelve Titans
nodes.symbolism: the divine light that makes precious things shine, the origin of all celestial luminosity, the Titaness whose children illuminate the world
nodes.neumann_archetype: the Great Mother in her luminous aspect, the feminine origin of all light and sight in the cosmos

nodes.name: Poena
nodes.physical_characteristics: spirit of punishment and retribution, often multiplied as the Poenae
nodes.significant_event: the divine punishment that follows wrongdoing, particularly the punishment for murder and blood-guilt
nodes.birth_circumstances: sometimes identified with or alongside the Erinyes
nodes.symbolism: retribution as an inescapable cosmic law, punishment as the consequence built into the fabric of the universe
nodes.neumann_archetype: the terrible feminine of cosmic retribution, punishment as the Great Mothers enforcement of blood-law

nodes.name: Pistis
nodes.physical_characteristics: personification of trust and good faith
nodes.significant_event: the spirit of trust that binds oaths and agreements, the divine quality that makes human society possible through mutual faith
nodes.symbolism: the foundation of all social bonds, trust as a sacred quality, the divine underpinning of human contracts and relationships
nodes.neumann_archetype: the positive feminine of reliability, the faith that binds consciousness into community

nodes.name: Potnia Theron
nodes.domain: wild animals, hunting, nature, the wilderness
nodes.character_trait: wild, sovereign over beasts, nurturing of animals, ancient
nodes.physical_characteristics: goddess flanked by wild animals, often lions or deer, sometimes winged, grasping animals in both hands
nodes.significant_event: depicted on Minoan seals and pottery from the earliest periods, Homer uses the title for Artemis, represents the most ancient layer of the hunting goddess
nodes.symbolism: the divine mistress of the animal world, the feminine as sovereign over wild nature, the goddess who both nurtures and hunts the beasts
nodes.neumann_archetype: the Great Mother in her most ancient theriomorphic aspect, the Lady of the Beasts who rules all animal nature

nodes.name: Sophrosyne
nodes.significant_event: one of the cardinal virtues of Greek philosophy, central to the ethics of Plato and Aristotle, the quality that allows humans to resist excess
nodes.symbolism: the golden mean between excess and deficiency, the self-knowledge that knows ones proper limits, the virtue that preserves the soul from the inflation of hybris
nodes.neumann_archetype: the conscious feminine restraint that prevents the ego from overreaching, the virtue of knowing the limits of consciousness

nodes.name: Praxidice
nodes.domain: justice, oaths, vengeance, execution of justice
nodes.physical_characteristics: goddess or triple goddesses of vengeance and just retribution
nodes.significant_event: worshipped at Haliartos in Boeotia as the enforcer of oaths and just punishment, associated with Persephone in some traditions
nodes.symbolism: the triple feminine principle of justice enforcement, the goddess who ensures oaths are kept through the threat of retribution
nodes.neumann_archetype: the triple Great Mother as the enforcer of cosmic law, the feminine principle that holds the patriarchal order to its own oaths

nodes.name: Potnia
nodes.domain: sovereignty, the Lady, divine feminine power, Mycenaean cult
nodes.physical_characteristics: the Lady or Mistress, a pre-Olympian sovereign goddess
nodes.significant_event: title found on Linear B tablets from Mycenaean Greece, possibly the supreme goddess of Mycenaean religion before the Olympian pantheon was established
nodes.symbolism: the absolute sovereignty of the pre-Olympian Great Goddess, the Lady whose very name was too sacred to elaborate, the unnamed feminine divine
nodes.neumann_archetype: the Great Mother as absolute sovereign, the pre-patriarchal feminine divine power before the Olympian reformation

nodes.name: Ptocheia
nodes.physical_characteristics: personification of beggary and extreme want
nodes.significant_event: the lowest extreme of material deprivation personified
nodes.symbolism: the abyss of poverty, destitution as a cosmic condition, the beggar as a figure of total deprivation
nodes.neumann_archetype: the shadow of abundance, the Great Mothers complete withholding

nodes.name: Rhapso
nodes.significant_event: presides over the hour of sewing and repair work
nodes.symbolism: the sacred dimension of textile repair, the patience of mending
nodes.neumann_archetype: the feminine of repair and restoration, the Great Mothers mending of the torn

nodes.name: Proioxis
nodes.domain: battle charge, the onset of battle, forward rush
nodes.physical_characteristics: spirit of the forward charge in battle
nodes.significant_event: the counter-force to Palioxis (Retreat), personification of the forward charge that drives an army against the enemy
nodes.birth_circumstances: associated with Ares and the battle daimons
nodes.symbolism: the momentum of the attack, the forward drive that overcomes fear and drives warriors into combat
nodes.neumann_archetype: the aggressive masculine drive toward engagement, the forward surge of martial consciousness

nodes.name: Prophasis
nodes.significant_event: personification of the pretext or excuse offered for wrongdoing
nodes.birth_circumstances: According to Pindar, she was the daughter of Epimetheus.
nodes.symbolism: the human capacity for self-justification, the excuse as a cosmic force opposing accountability
nodes.neumann_archetype: the shadow of consciousness that avoids responsibility through rationalization

nodes.name: Telete
nodes.physical_characteristics: personification of the mystery initiation itself
nodes.significant_event: personification of the initiation rite (telete) at the heart of the Greek mystery religions, the experience of divine transformation through ritual
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughter of Dionysus and Nicaea in some traditions
nodes.symbolism: the mystery of initiation as a divine being, the transformation that occurs through sacred ritual, the unspeakable experience at the heart of the Mysteries
nodes.neumann_archetype: the feminine mystery of transformation itself, initiation as the Great Mothers transformative encounter with consciousness

nodes.name: Planē
nodes.significant_event: personification of going astray in both physical and moral senses
nodes.symbolism: the cosmic force that leads mortals off the true path, error as a divine affliction
nodes.neumann_archetype: the shadow of consciousness that leads away from truth, the wandering that precedes finding

nodes.name: Soteria
nodes.physical_characteristics: personification of safety and deliverance from danger
nodes.significant_event: worshipped after successful escapes from danger or victory in battle, festivals of Soteria held at Delphi after the Gauls were repelled
nodes.symbolism: the divine gift of salvation from danger, deliverance as a cosmic grace, the gratitude owed for rescue from peril
nodes.neumann_archetype: the positive feminine of preservation and rescue, safety as a gift of the divine

nodes.name: Sponde
nodes.significant_event: presides over the hour of ritual libation, the pouring of offerings to the gods
nodes.symbolism: the sacred act of pouring offerings, the libation as the connection between mortal and divine
nodes.neumann_archetype: the feminine of ritual offering, consciousness pouring itself out to the transpersonal

nodes.name: Achilles
nodes.animals: snake, horse, dog, bear, phoenix, centaur
nodes.character_trait: wrathful, proud, brave, loyal, honorable, swift
nodes.significant_event: withdraws from battle over dishonor from Agamemnon, returns after Patroclus is killed by Hector, slays Hector and drags his body around Troy, killed by Paris with an arrow to his heel
nodes.birth_circumstances: The central character in Homer's Iliad, he was the son of the Nereid Thetis and Peleus, king of Phthia and famous Argonaut.
nodes.symbolism: the tension between glory and mortality, the cost of wrath, the hero whose invulnerability has a fatal flaw
nodes.neumann_archetype: the hero in his wrathful and mortal aspect, the son who must die young to achieve eternal glory

nodes.name: Aeneas
nodes.domain: duty, piety, founding of Rome, exile, destiny
nodes.physical_characteristics: tall, handsome Trojan warrior, carrying his father on his back from burning Troy
nodes.significant_event: escaped the fall of Troy carrying his aged father Anchises and leading his son Ascanius, wandered the Mediterranean, loved and abandoned Dido queen of Carthage, descended to the underworld, founded the line that would establish Rome
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of the Trojan prince Anchises and the goddess Aphrodite, born on Mount Ida
nodes.symbolism: duty and destiny over personal desire, the exile who founds a greater civilization, piety as the supreme virtue, the bridge between the Greek and Roman worlds
nodes.neumann_archetype: the hero of destiny who sacrifices personal happiness (Dido) for the collective fate of founding a new civilization

nodes.name: Agamemnon
nodes.physical_characteristics: broad-chested king, tallest among the Achaeans
nodes.significant_event: led the Greek forces against Troy, sacrificed his daughter Iphigenia for favorable winds, murdered by his wife Clytemnestra and her lover Aegisthus upon his return home
nodes.birth_circumstances: Agamemnon was a descendant of Pelops, son of Tantalus.
nodes.symbolism: the corrupting nature of absolute power, the curse that follows bloodshed within a royal house
nodes.neumann_archetype: the patriarch whose hubris brings destruction upon his own house

nodes.name: Ajax the Lesser
nodes.object: spear, thunderbolt, trident, helmet, shield, sword
nodes.physical_characteristics: smaller than his namesake but swift and fierce, skilled with the spear
nodes.significant_event: raped Cassandra in the temple of Athena during the sack of Troy, punished by Athena who wrecked his fleet with storms on the voyage home, drowned clinging to a rock after boasting that he survived against the gods will
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of Oileus king of Locris
nodes.symbolism: impiety and its consequences, the warrior whose skill cannot save him from divine retribution, the violation of sanctuary as the worst sin
nodes.neumann_archetype: the shadow hero who violates the sacred feminine (Athenas temple) and is destroyed by the offended goddess

nodes.name: Ajax the Great
nodes.physical_characteristics: colossal, towering over other warriors, the tallest of the Greeks after Achilles
nodes.significant_event: the bulwark of the Greek army, fought Hector to a draw, competed with Odysseus for Achilles armor and lost, went mad and killed himself in shame
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of King Telamon of Salamis and Periboea, half-brother of Teucer
nodes.symbolism: the tragedy of the warrior whose valor is not recognized, brute strength defeated by cunning intelligence, honor as fatal pride
nodes.neumann_archetype: the hero of pure strength who is destroyed when confronted by the claims of consciousness (Odysseus) over brute force

nodes.name: Atalanta
nodes.physical_characteristics: beautiful, athletic huntress, the swiftest of all mortals
nodes.significant_event: drew first blood against the Calydonian Boar, defeated all suitors in foot races until Hippomenes used golden apples from Aphrodite to distract her, both transformed into lions for profaning a temple
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughter of Iasus or Schoeneus and Clymene, exposed at birth because her father wanted a son, nursed by a she-bear sent by Artemis
nodes.symbolism: the autonomous feminine warrior, the race that no man can win without divine trickery, the punishment for violating sacred space
nodes.neumann_archetype: the Artemis-like feminine who resists integration with the masculine, the wild huntress who must be tricked rather than conquered

nodes.name: Academus
nodes.physical_characteristics: Attic hero associated with a sacred grove
nodes.significant_event: revealed to Castor and Pollux where Theseus had hidden their sister Helen, his sacred grove near Athens became the site of Platos Academy
nodes.symbolism: wisdom transmitted through sacred place, the grove as site of philosophical inquiry
nodes.neumann_archetype: the wise elder whose sacred space becomes the seat of consciousness and reason

nodes.name: Amphiaraus
nodes.domain: prophecy, war, the underworld, divine favor
nodes.physical_characteristics: seer and warrior who foresaw his own death
nodes.significant_event: foresaw his own death if he joined the Seven against Thebes but was forced to go by his wife Eriphyle who was bribed with Harmonias necklace, swallowed alive by the earth during battle through Zeus intervention
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of Oicles, a prophet descended from the seer Melampus
nodes.symbolism: the prophet who knows his fate but cannot escape it, the seer whose wife betrays him for gold, divine intervention as both destruction and salvation
nodes.neumann_archetype: the prophetic hero swallowed by the earth (Great Mother) rather than killed in battle, suggesting a return to the maternal ground

nodes.name: Antilochus
nodes.physical_characteristics: young and handsome warrior, son of Nestor
nodes.significant_event: sacrificed his life at Troy to save his father Nestor from the Ethiopian king Memnon, his death prompted Achilles to fight and kill Memnon
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of King Nestor of Pylos, one of the youngest Greek warriors at Troy
nodes.symbolism: the son who dies to save the father, youth sacrificed in war, filial devotion as the highest virtue
nodes.neumann_archetype: the sacrificial son who reverses the usual pattern by giving his life for the father rather than opposing him

nodes.name: Abderus
nodes.significant_event: left by Heracles to guard the man-eating Mares of Diomedes during the Eighth Labor, was devoured by the mares, Heracles founded the city of Abdera in his honor
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of Hermes according to some traditions, or of Opian
nodes.symbolism: the cost of the heros quest paid by his companions, the founding sacrifice that establishes a city
nodes.neumann_archetype: the sacrificial companion of the hero whose death becomes the founding act of civilization

nodes.name: Asteropaios
nodes.physical_characteristics: mighty Paeonian warrior allied with Troy, descended from the river Axius
nodes.significant_event: challenged Achilles in single combat at Troy, the only warrior to wound Achilles leg, ultimately killed by Achilles who mocked his river lineage
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of the river god Axius and the nymph Periboea
nodes.symbolism: the barbarian warrior whose river-god ancestry cannot save him from the greatest Greek hero, the limits of divine blood against fate
nodes.neumann_archetype: the river-born hero who challenges the supreme masculine but falls to the hero of fate

nodes.name: Athis
nodes.significant_event: killed in battle alongside his companions
nodes.birth_circumstances: In Book V of Ovid's mock-epic Metamorphoses, Athis is a young demigod of outstanding beauty from India, son of Limnaee, a nymph of the Ganges.
nodes.symbolism: the beauty of youth consumed by war, the loyal companion who falls
nodes.neumann_archetype: the beautiful youth sacrificed in the flames of war

nodes.name: Alcathous
nodes.physical_characteristics: prince of Elis who redeemed himself through heroic deeds
nodes.significant_event: slew the lion of Cithaeron and won the hand of Evaechme daughter of Megareus king of Megara
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of King Pelops and Hippodamia, brother of Atreus and Thyestes
nodes.symbolism: the son who escapes the family curse through individual heroic labor
nodes.neumann_archetype: the hero who breaks free of the ancestral curse through personal achievement

nodes.name: Alexanor
nodes.physical_characteristics: grandson of Asclepius worshipped as a healing hero
nodes.significant_event: established a temple and healing shrine to his grandfather Asclepius at Titane in Sicyon
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of Machaon, grandson of Asclepius
nodes.symbolism: the transmission of healing knowledge through generations, the hero cult as the foundation of medicine
nodes.neumann_archetype: the grandson who perpetuates the healing tradition of the Great Physician

nodes.name: Bellerophon
nodes.physical_characteristics: handsome hero riding the winged horse Pegasus
nodes.significant_event: tamed Pegasus with a golden bridle given by Athena, slew the Chimera from the air on Pegasuss back, attempted to fly to Olympus but was thrown down by Zeus and wandered crippled and alone
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of Poseidon and Eurynome, raised as foster son of Glaucus king of Corinth
nodes.symbolism: the hero who rises too high, the danger of mortal hubris in seeking divine status, the winged horse as the vehicle of transcendence that can also destroy
nodes.neumann_archetype: the hero who achieves the heights of consciousness but is destroyed by his attempt to transcend human limits

nodes.name: Andropompus
nodes.physical_characteristics: hero or daemon who drives away evil
nodes.significant_event: worshipped as a protector who drives away pollution and evil spirits from communities
nodes.birth_circumstances: In Greek mythology, Andropompus (Ancient Greek: Ἀνδρόπομπος) was one of the descendants of Neleus, king of Thessaly, as son of Penthilus and Anchirhoe.
nodes.symbolism: the heroic function of driving away spiritual pollution, purification as heroic labor
nodes.neumann_archetype: the protective masculine that cleanses the community of dangerous spiritual forces

nodes.name: Aratus
nodes.significant_event: worshipped as a healing hero, associated with the spread of the Asclepian healing cult
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of the god Asclepius and the mortal Aristodeme of Sicyon
nodes.symbolism: the divine healing tradition passed through mortal lineage
nodes.neumann_archetype: the son who carries the fathers healing legacy into mortal communities

nodes.name: Anagyros
nodes.physical_characteristics: local Attic hero with a sacred grove
nodes.significant_event: an old man who cut down trees in his sacred grove was cursed, giving rise to the proverb do not move Anagyros meaning do not provoke a sleeping evil
nodes.birth_circumstances: Angered, the concubine reported back to the old man and falsely accused the son of sexually assaulting her.
nodes.symbolism: the sanctity of sacred groves, the slumbering hero whose anger must not be provoked
nodes.neumann_archetype: the chthonic hero whose wrath guards the sacred trees of the Great Mother

nodes.name: Cadmus
nodes.domain: civilization, writing, founding of cities, the alphabet
nodes.physical_characteristics: Phoenician prince, founder hero of Thebes
nodes.significant_event: slew the dragon sacred to Ares at the future site of Thebes, sowed its teeth which grew into armed warriors (the Spartoi), founded Thebes, brought the Phoenician alphabet to Greece, transformed into a serpent in old age
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of King Agenor and Queen Telephassa of Tyre, brother of Europa
nodes.symbolism: the transmission of writing and civilization from East to West, the founding of cities from violence (the sown teeth), the curse that follows the slaying of the sacred
nodes.neumann_archetype: the culture hero who brings the tools of consciousness (writing) from the older civilization to the new

nodes.name: Erechtheus
nodes.physical_characteristics: early king of Athens, sometimes confused with or identified as Erichthonius
nodes.significant_event: sacrificed his daughter to save Athens during war with Eleusis, receiving an oracle that demanded such sacrifice, swallowed by the earth after his victory
nodes.birth_circumstances: autochthonous (earth-born) king of Athens, or son of Pandion I
nodes.death_circumstances: In the following battle between the forces of Athens and Eleusis, Erechtheus won the battle and slew Eumolpus, but then himself fell, struck down by Poseidon's trident.
nodes.symbolism: the earth-born king who returns to the earth, the ruler who sacrifices his own family for the city, Athenian autochthony
nodes.neumann_archetype: the earth-born hero-king who is reclaimed by the Great Mother, the patriarch who sacrifices the feminine (daughter) for the collective

nodes.name: Cecrops I
nodes.physical_characteristics: half-human with serpent body below the waist, born from the earth itself
nodes.significant_event: founded Athens and judged the contest between Athena and Poseidon for patronage of the city choosing Athena, established laws of marriage, burial, and writing, ended human sacrifice
nodes.birth_circumstances: autochthonous (earth-born), the first king of Attica
nodes.symbolism: the earth-born king, civilization emerging from the chthonic, the serpent-king who bridges the primordial and the civilized
nodes.neumann_archetype: the autochthonous culture hero, born from the Great Mother (earth) to establish masculine civilization, retaining his chthonic serpent nature

nodes.name: Ceryx
nodes.physical_characteristics: first herald, carrying a herald staff (kerykeion)
nodes.significant_event: founded the clan of the Kerykes (Heralds) at Eleusis who held hereditary priesthoods in the Eleusinian Mysteries
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of Hermes and one of the daughters of Cecrops, or son of Eumolpus
nodes.symbolism: the sacred function of the herald, divine speech as a hereditary gift, the messenger tradition as sacred lineage
nodes.neumann_archetype: the son of the divine messenger who establishes the human tradition of sacred communication

nodes.name: Diomedes
nodes.object: spear, shield, chariot, armor of gold
nodes.character_trait: brave, fierce, pious, favored by Athena, fearless even against gods
nodes.physical_characteristics: powerful warrior, one of the youngest and most formidable Greek champions at Troy
nodes.significant_event: wounded both Aphrodite and Ares in battle at Troy with Athenas aid, exchanged armor with the Lycian Glaucus, one of the warriors inside the Trojan Horse, returned safely home from Troy
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of Tydeus and Deipyle, grandson of Adrastus, king of Argos
nodes.symbolism: the mortal warrior empowered by divine favor to challenge even the gods, courage that transcends human limits when guided by wisdom
nodes.neumann_archetype: the hero empowered by the positive anima (Athena) to confront the dark powers directly, one of the few who wounds gods and returns whole

nodes.name: Caeneus
nodes.physical_characteristics: born female (Caenis) but transformed into an invulnerable man by Poseidon
nodes.significant_event: born as the maiden Caenis, raped by Poseidon who granted any wish, asked to become a man and be made invulnerable, killed by Centaurs who buried him under tree trunks since he could not be pierced
nodes.birth_circumstances: Caeneus was born a girl, Caenis (), the daughter of Elatus, but after Poseidon had sex with Caenis, she was transformed by him into an invulnerable man.
nodes.death_circumstances: Caeneus' son was the Argonaut Coronus, who was killed by Heracles while leading a war against the Dorians and their king Aegimius.
nodes.symbolism: gender transformation as divine gift, invulnerability as compensation for violation, the buried hero who cannot be conventionally killed
nodes.neumann_archetype: the feminine transformed to masculine by the sea god, the invulnerable hero whose strength was born from the violation of the feminine

nodes.name: Electryone
nodes.physical_characteristics: radiant maiden associated with the dawn
nodes.significant_event: died as a virgin and was honored as a heroine, associated with the rising sun and the awakening of the world
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughter of Helios (Sun) and Rhode, or another nymph
nodes.symbolism: the maiden of dawn, the light that awakens the world each morning, virginal radiance
nodes.neumann_archetype: the luminous maiden archetype, the daughter of the sun as the dawn of consciousness

nodes.name: Evander of Pallantium
nodes.physical_characteristics: Arcadian hero who founded the settlement on the Palatine Hill in Rome
nodes.significant_event: led a group of Arcadian colonists to Italy, founded a settlement on the Palatine Hill sixty years before the Trojan War, introduced writing and music to the Italian natives
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of Hermes and an Arcadian nymph Themis (or Nicostrate/Carmenta)
nodes.symbolism: the Greek civilizing mission to the west, the Arcadian origins of Roman culture, the bearer of writing and law to the barbarian world
nodes.neumann_archetype: the culture hero who carries consciousness (writing, music, law) from the Greek center to the western frontier

nodes.name: Euphorbus
nodes.domain: the Trojan War, reincarnation, Pythagorean philosophy
nodes.physical_characteristics: the most beautiful of the Trojan warriors
nodes.significant_event: killed Patroclus alongside Hector but was then slain by Menelaus, Pythagoras later claimed to be the reincarnation of Euphorbus and recognized his shield in the temple of Hera at Argos
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of Panthous, a Trojan elder
nodes.death_circumstances: In the Iliad Euphorbus wounded Patroclus before the Achaean hero was killed by Hector, and was then killed by Menelaus in the fight for Patroclus' body.
nodes.symbolism: the beautiful warrior whose death connects to the philosophical doctrine of reincarnation, the soul that transmigrates across the ages
nodes.neumann_archetype: the beautiful masculine slain in battle whose soul endures through reincarnation, the bridge between the heroic and philosophical ages

nodes.name: Ganymede
nodes.domain: youth, beauty, cupbearer of the gods, divine desire
nodes.physical_characteristics: the most beautiful of mortal youths, young Trojan prince
nodes.significant_event: abducted by Zeus in the form of an eagle (or by the eagle) to serve as cupbearer on Olympus, replacing Hebe, his father received divine horses as compensation
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of King Tros of Troy (or Laomedon), descended from Dardanus and Zeus
nodes.symbolism: divine desire for mortal beauty, the boy snatched up to heaven, immortality granted through beauty rather than heroic deeds, the origin of the constellation Aquarius
nodes.neumann_archetype: the beautiful youth seized by the sky father, the passive masculine absorbed into the divine through beauty rather than action

nodes.name: Glaucus
nodes.domain: the sea, prophecy, transformation, fishing, herbs
nodes.physical_characteristics: sea god with fish tail and seaweed hair, green-skinned
nodes.significant_event: ate a magical herb that made fish come alive, threw himself into the sea and was transformed into a sea god by Oceanus and Tethys, became a prophetic deity consulted by sailors
nodes.birth_circumstances: originally a mortal fisherman or son of the sea deities Nereus and Thetis
nodes.death_circumstances: Later in the war, when the fighting over Achilles' corpse took place, Glaucus was killed by Ajax.
nodes.symbolism: transformation from mortal to divine through contact with the magical herb, the fisherman who becomes a fish-god, the sea as the realm of prophetic wisdom
nodes.neumann_archetype: the masculine transformed through consuming the Great Mothers magical vegetation, the mortal absorbed into the oceanic unconscious and emerging as a prophet

nodes.name: Eunostus
nodes.character_trait: just, protective of women, vengeful when wronged
nodes.significant_event: murdered by his kinswomen for his virtue toward women, avenged by a plague until his cult was established
nodes.birth_circumstances: His parents were Elieus, son of Cephissus, and Scias.
nodes.symbolism: the virtuous man destroyed by the very group he protects, the hero cult born from unjust murder
nodes.neumann_archetype: the positive masculine destroyed by the shadow feminine, whose death establishes a new sacred order

nodes.name: Eurytus and Cteatus
nodes.physical_characteristics: conjoined or twin warriors of supernatural strength, joined at the hip in some versions
nodes.significant_event: defeated Heracles in battle at Cleonae, later killed treacherously by Heracles at a truce, their joint strength made them nearly invincible
nodes.birth_circumstances: sons of Poseidon (or Actor) and Molione
nodes.death_circumstances: However after the latter made peace, the brothers attacked Heracles and were subsequently killed by him outside Cleonae.
nodes.symbolism: the power of twinned warriors, the inseparable bond that makes ordinary men superhuman, the hero (Heracles) who must resort to treachery against united strength
nodes.neumann_archetype: the divine twins as the doubled masculine, the hero pattern reflected and doubled into invincibility

nodes.name: Coön
nodes.physical_characteristics: Trojan warrior and elder son of Antenor
nodes.significant_event: attacked Agamemnon with a spear to avenge his brother Iphidamas, wounded Agamemnon but was killed by him
nodes.birth_circumstances: eldest son of the Trojan elder Antenor
nodes.symbolism: the elder brother who dies avenging the younger, the futility of revenge in the face of superior arms
nodes.neumann_archetype: the protective eldest son whose vengeance against the patriarchal enemy leads to his own destruction

nodes.name: Ceraon
nodes.significant_event: credited with the invention of the pottery craft or credited with innovations in ceramic technique
nodes.symbolism: the divine origin of the potters craft, earth transformed by fire into vessels
nodes.neumann_archetype: the culture hero who transforms the raw matter of the Great Mother (clay) through fire

nodes.name: Deipneus
nodes.physical_characteristics: hero associated with the art of feasting
nodes.significant_event: credited with innovations in cuisine and banquet preparation
nodes.symbolism: the sacred art of hospitality and the divine dimension of the feast
nodes.neumann_archetype: the culture hero of the domestic arts, the masculine ordering of the social meal

nodes.name: Eurybarus
nodes.significant_event: credited with feats of strength in local tradition
nodes.birth_circumstances: Eurybarus or Eurybaros (Ancient Greek: Εὐρύβαρος), Eurybatos (Εὐρύβατος) or Eurybates (Εὐρυβάτης) was a Greek mythological hero, son of Euphemus and a descendant of the river god Axios.
nodes.symbolism: the heroic embodiment of physical power
nodes.neumann_archetype: the purely physical hero expressing undifferentiated masculine strength

nodes.name: Euxynthetus
nodes.physical_characteristics: Athenian hero associated with technical innovation
nodes.significant_event: credited with innovations in craftsmanship in Attic tradition
nodes.symbolism: the inventive spirit of Athenian craft traditions
nodes.neumann_archetype: the culture hero as inventor of practical arts

nodes.name: Hector
nodes.object: chariot, shield, spear, sword, arrow, helmet
nodes.character_trait: brave, noble, devoted to family, dutiful, honorable
nodes.physical_characteristics: tall, bearded warrior, the greatest champion of Troy
nodes.significant_event: the greatest Trojan warrior who defended his city against the Greeks, killed Patroclus in battle, slain by Achilles who dragged his body behind his chariot, his body ransomed by Priam
nodes.birth_circumstances: eldest son of King Priam and Queen Hecuba of Troy, brother of Paris
nodes.symbolism: duty to family and city above personal safety, the noble defender doomed to fall, the tragedy of war that destroys the best on both sides
nodes.neumann_archetype: the hero bound to the collective rather than the individual quest, the defender archetype who fights not for glory but for home

nodes.name: Jason
nodes.physical_characteristics: handsome hero wearing one sandal, leader of the Argonauts
nodes.significant_event: led the Argonauts to Colchis to retrieve the Golden Fleece, won it with Medeas help, betrayed Medea for Glauce of Corinth leading to the murder of his children, died alone beneath the rotting Argo
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of Aeson, the rightful king of Iolcos, raised by the centaur Chiron
nodes.symbolism: the quest hero who succeeds through others power rather than his own, the betrayal of the feminine helper, ambition that leads to ruin
nodes.neumann_archetype: the hero who relies on the anima (Medea) for his quest but betrays the feminine, leading to catastrophic reversal

nodes.name: Odysseus
nodes.character_trait: cunning, resourceful, eloquent, enduring, deceptive, loyal to home
nodes.physical_characteristics: short but broad-shouldered, auburn-haired, scarred on the thigh by a boar
nodes.significant_event: devised the Trojan Horse to end the Trojan War, wandered ten years facing Cyclops Polyphemus and Circe and Scylla and the Sirens, returned home to slay the suitors of Penelope
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of Laertes and Anticlea, king of Ithaca, though some traditions name Sisyphus as his true father
nodes.symbolism: the triumph of intelligence over brute force, the longing for home as the deepest human drive, the hero who survives through cunning rather than strength
nodes.neumann_archetype: the hero of consciousness who navigates the perils of the unconscious (sea monsters, enchantresses, the underworld) through intelligence and endurance

nodes.name: Menelaus
nodes.domain: kingship, the Trojan War, marital honor, Sparta
nodes.character_trait: wronged, devoted, brave but secondary to his brother, persistent
nodes.physical_characteristics: red-haired in some traditions, strong warrior though not the equal of Achilles or Ajax
nodes.significant_event: husband of Helen whose abduction by Paris caused the Trojan War, defeated Paris in single combat but Paris was saved by Aphrodite, reunited with Helen after the fall of Troy
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of Atreus and Aerope, brother of Agamemnon, king of Sparta
nodes.symbolism: the wronged husband whose personal grievance launches a civilization-defining war, honor that demands the destruction of a city, the man who gets his wife back but at what cost
nodes.neumann_archetype: the patriarchal masculine whose possession of the anima (Helen) is challenged by the erotic masculine (Paris), requiring the entire hero-world to restore the patriarchal order

nodes.name: Hippothoon
nodes.physical_characteristics: Attic hero and king, ancestor of the Hippothontid tribe
nodes.significant_event: his mother was killed by her father Cercyon for her pregnancy, Hippothoon was exposed but nursed by a mare and eventually became king and the eponymous hero of the Attic tribe Hippothontis
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of Poseidon and Alope daughter of Cercyon
nodes.symbolism: the exposed child who survives through divine intervention (the nurturing mare), the hero who rises from abandonment to kingship
nodes.neumann_archetype: the divine child abandoned by the human father, nurtured by the animal aspect of the Great Mother (the mare), and rising to sovereign power

nodes.name: Iphigenia
nodes.domain: sacrifice, purity, the transition from human to divine
nodes.physical_characteristics: beautiful young princess, maiden of noble bearing
nodes.significant_event: sacrificed by her father Agamemnon at Aulis so the Greek fleet could sail to Troy, in some versions Artemis substituted a deer at the last moment and transported Iphigenia to Tauris as her priestess
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughter of King Agamemnon and Queen Clytemnestra of Mycenae
nodes.death_circumstances: In some versions, such as Hyginus's Fabulae, Iphigenia is not sacrificed.
nodes.symbolism: the innocent sacrifice demanded by divine power, the father who kills his daughter for political ambition, the maiden transformed through sacrifice into priestess
nodes.neumann_archetype: the sacrificed maiden archetype, the daughter offered to appease the Terrible Mother (Artemis) so the patriarchal quest (Troy) may proceed

nodes.name: Idomeneus
nodes.domain: kingship, war, the Cretan alliance at Troy
nodes.physical_characteristics: elderly but mighty warrior, grandson of Minos
nodes.significant_event: led the Cretan contingent of eighty ships to Troy, a suitor of Helen, killed many Trojans but upon returning home found his wife unfaithful and was driven into exile
nodes.birth_circumstances: grandson of King Minos of Crete, son of Deucalion
nodes.symbolism: the aging warrior whose victories abroad cannot prevent betrayal at home, the Cretan kings fall from glory, the futility of heroism when domestic order is lost
nodes.neumann_archetype: the aging hero-king whose warrior achievements cannot protect him from the faithless anima at home

nodes.name: Forseti
nodes.birth_circumstances: According to Snorri Sturluson in the Prose Edda, Forseti is the son of Baldr and Nanna.

nodes.name: Meleager
nodes.physical_characteristics: powerful hunter and warrior of Calydon
nodes.significant_event: led the hunt against the Calydonian Boar sent by Artemis, gave the boar hide to Atalanta causing a quarrel in which he killed his uncles, his mother Althaea burned the brand that held his life and he died
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of King Oeneus of Calydon and Althaea, or of the god Ares, his life was tied to a brand in the fire by the Fates at his birth
nodes.symbolism: fate bound to a physical object, the mothers power over the sons life, honor and passion leading to destruction
nodes.neumann_archetype: the hero whose life is literally held by the Great Mother (the brand), destroyed when the mother exercises her terrible power

nodes.name: Hyacinth
nodes.domain: vegetation, beauty, rebirth, male beauty, spring
nodes.character_trait: beautiful, beloved, tragic, reborn as a flower
nodes.physical_characteristics: most beautiful of mortal youths, Spartan prince
nodes.significant_event: beloved of Apollo who accidentally killed him with a discus, or Zephyrus jealously redirected the discus, from his blood sprang the hyacinth flower inscribed with the letters AI (a cry of grief)
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of King Amyclas of Sparta and Diomede
nodes.symbolism: beauty destroyed by accident or jealousy, the dying god who returns as a flower, the blood that generates new life, the pre-Hellenic vegetation deity
nodes.neumann_archetype: the beautiful youth killed by the masculine god, the dying and rising vegetation deity who transforms death into perennial flowering

nodes.name: Messene
nodes.domain: city founding, regional identity, the Peloponnese
nodes.physical_characteristics: heroine who gave her name to the region of Messenia
nodes.significant_event: left Argos with her husband Polycaon and established the kingdom of Messenia in the southwestern Peloponnese, bringing the Eleusinian Mysteries to the region
nodes.birth_circumstances: daughter of King Triopas of Argos, wife of Polycaon
nodes.symbolism: the princess who founds a new kingdom, the transmission of sacred mysteries to new lands, the feminine as the carrier of civilization
nodes.neumann_archetype: the founding heroine who carries the mysteries of the Great Mother to a new region

nodes.name: Memnon
nodes.physical_characteristics: most beautiful of warriors, with dark skin and golden armor
nodes.significant_event: came to Troy as an ally with a great Ethiopian army, killed Antilochus but was then killed by Achilles, Zeus granted him immortality at his mothers tears, his men were turned into birds (Memnonides) that visit his tomb annually
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of Eos (Dawn) and the mortal Tithonus, king of Ethiopia
nodes.symbolism: the dawn-born hero who falls to the greatest warrior, beauty and nobility in death, the mothers grief that wins immortality for her son
nodes.neumann_archetype: the son of the dawn goddess whose beauty and death embody the tragic hero at the threshold of light and dark

nodes.name: Nisus and Euryalus
nodes.domain: friendship, loyalty in war, heroic companionship
nodes.physical_characteristics: two young Trojan warriors, close friends
nodes.significant_event: made a night raid on the sleeping Rutulian camp but Euryalus was captured and killed when the moonlight glinted on his stolen helmet, Nisus died trying to save him
nodes.birth_circumstances: Nisus elder and more experienced, Euryalus younger and beautiful
nodes.symbolism: the bond of warrior friendship stronger than the fear of death, the beautiful youth whose love of spoils causes both their deaths, devotion unto death
nodes.neumann_archetype: the doubled hero who fights and dies as one, the masculine bond that transcends individual survival

nodes.name: Maron
nodes.physical_characteristics: old priest or companion of Dionysus

nodes.birth_circumstances: son of Silenus, or son of Dionysus himself
nodes.symbolism: the priestly tradition of winemaking, the old companion who carries the gods wisdom of the vine
nodes.neumann_archetype: the silenic wise man of the Dionysiac circle, the priestly masculine who mediates between the wine god and humanity

nodes.name: Mesthles
nodes.significant_event: led the Maeonian contingent at Troy alongside his brother Antiphus
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of Talaimenes, leader of the Maeonians
nodes.symbolism: the allied warrior whose distant homeland answers the call to defend Troy
nodes.neumann_archetype: the peripheral hero drawn into the central conflict of the age

nodes.name: Nannacus
nodes.physical_characteristics: ancient king who wept for the destruction he foresaw

nodes.birth_circumstances: king of Iconium in Phrygia
nodes.symbolism: the prophet-king who can only weep at the approaching catastrophe he cannot prevent, excessive foreknowledge as torment
nodes.neumann_archetype: the prophetic consciousness overwhelmed by knowledge of the approaching destruction, the king whose tears cannot avert the flood

nodes.name: Menestratus
nodes.physical_characteristics: young hero who sacrificed himself for his city or beloved

nodes.symbolism: the voluntary sacrifice of the hero for the community, love expressed through self-destruction
nodes.neumann_archetype: the sacrificial hero who gives himself for the collective, the highest expression of masculine devotion

nodes.name: Peleus

nodes.object: spear of ash, wedding gifts from the gods
nodes.physical_characteristics: mortal king and warrior, father of Achilles

nodes.birth_circumstances: son of Aeacus king of Aegina and the nymph Endeis
nodes.symbolism: the mortal who must wrestle the divine feminine through all her transformations, the wedding that triggers the Trojan War, the father of the greatest warrior who outlives his son
nodes.neumann_archetype: the hero who seizes the shape-shifting anima and holds her through all transformations, the mortal father of the doomed divine-mortal son

nodes.name: Oedipus
nodes.physical_characteristics: pierced and swollen feet from infancy, later blind and ragged as an exile
nodes.significant_event: solved the riddle of the Sphinx saving Thebes, unknowingly killed his father and married his mother fulfilling the prophecy, blinded himself upon discovering the truth, died at Colonus

nodes.symbolism: the inescapability of fate, the tragic cost of self-knowledge, the riddle of human identity, blindness as the price of seeing the truth
nodes.neumann_archetype: the hero whose quest for truth leads to the destruction of the ego, the solver of the Sphinxs riddle who cannot solve the riddle of himself

nodes.name: Orestes
nodes.domain: matricide, justice, purification, the transition from blood vengeance to law
nodes.physical_characteristics: young prince haunted by the Furies
nodes.significant_event: killed his mother Clytemnestra to avenge his fathers murder, pursued by the Erinyes for matricide, tried and acquitted at Athens by the court of the Areopagus with Athenas casting vote
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of Agamemnon and Clytemnestra, brother of Electra and Iphigenia
nodes.symbolism: the transition from the archaic law of blood vengeance to civic justice, the impossible conflict between duty to father and duty to mother, purification through institutional law
nodes.neumann_archetype: the hero caught between the matriarchal (Erinyes) and patriarchal (Apollo) orders, resolved by the emergence of civic consciousness (Athena)

nodes.name: Phoroneus

nodes.symbolism: the first mortal king, the discovery of fire as the foundation of civilization, the river-born first man of the Argolid
nodes.neumann_archetype: the first conscious man born from the river (the Great Mother), the founding patriarch who receives fire (consciousness)

nodes.name: Protesilaus

nodes.physical_characteristics: young warrior who leaped first from the Greek ships onto Trojan soil

nodes.birth_circumstances: son of Iphicles king of Phylace in Thessaly
nodes.death_circumstances: An oracle by Thetis had prophesied that the first Greek to walk on the land after stepping off a ship in the Trojan War would be the first to die, he was himself slain by Hector.
nodes.symbolism: the willing sacrifice of being first, the threshold hero who pays the price of initiation, love that transcends death, the first step onto hostile ground
nodes.neumann_archetype: the sacrificial hero who crosses the threshold first, paying with his life to open the way for the collective

nodes.name: Patroclus
nodes.physical_characteristics: strong and compassionate warrior, wearing borrowed armor

nodes.birth_circumstances: son of Menoetius, raised alongside Achilles in the house of Peleus after accidentally killing a playmate
nodes.symbolism: the devoted friend whose death is the catalyst for the greatest warriors return, borrowed identity (Achilles armor) as both strength and doom, friendship as the deepest bond of the heroic world
nodes.neumann_archetype: the alter ego or shadow of the supreme hero, the gentle masculine whose death reactivates the terrible masculine (Achilles)

nodes.name: Podalirius
nodes.domain: healing, medicine, the Trojan War, Asclepian tradition
nodes.significant_event: served as physician to the Greeks at Troy, specialized in internal medicine while his brother Machaon was a surgeon, after the war established healing centers
nodes.birth_circumstances: son of Asclepius and Epione, brother of Machaon
nodes.symbolism: the medical tradition descended from the divine healer, internal medicine as a divine art, the healer-warrior who saves rather than destroys
nodes.neumann_archetype: the son of the Great Healer who carries the internal medicine tradition, the masculine that preserves life within the context of war

nodes.name: Parthenopaeus

nodes.birth_circumstances: son of Atalanta and either Meleager or Hippomenes, exposed at birth and suckled by a she-bear

nodes.symbolism: the child of the huntress raised by wild nature, the doomed hero who inherits his mothers wildness and his fathers fate
nodes.neumann_archetype: the hero born of the masculine-feminine (Atalanta the hunter-maiden), raised by the animal mother (bear), fated to die in the assault on the patriarchal city

nodes.name: Pelops

nodes.symbolism: the generational curse that follows betrayal, resurrection and divine favor, the original sin that dooms an entire royal line
nodes.neumann_archetype: the dismembered and resurrected son, the founding figure whose transgression initiates the tragic cycle of the patriarchal house

nodes.name: Perseus

nodes.symbolism: the hero who conquers terror through reflection rather than direct confrontation, divine favor enabling the impossible quest, the mirror as consciousness facing the unconscious
nodes.neumann_archetype: the hero who defeats the Terrible Mother (Medusa) by using the mirror of consciousness, the archetypal dragon-slayer

nodes.name: Othryoneus

nodes.symbolism: youthful hubris attempting to wield divine power, the catastrophe of exceeding mortal limits, the son who must prove his fathers identity at the cost of his life
nodes.neumann_archetype: the failed solar hero who cannot bear the burden of full consciousness, destroyed by the very light he sought to command

nodes.name: The Earth Mother
nodes.domain: earth, agriculture, childbirth, nourishment, the dead
nodes.physical_characteristics: maternal figure associated with the fertile earth, sometimes depicted pregnant or nursing
nodes.significant_event: appears across traditions as Gaia, Terra, Pachamama, Nerthus, Prithvi, receiving the dead and bringing forth the living
nodes.symbolism: the earth as living maternal body, the cycle of sowing and harvest as birth and death, the ground that receives and regenerates
nodes.neumann_archetype: the Good Mother aspect of the Great Mother, the nourishing earth

nodes.name: The Primordial Waters
nodes.physical_characteristics: boundless dark waters existing before creation, sometimes personified as a serpent or dragon
nodes.significant_event: from the primordial waters creation emerges across Nun (Egyptian), Apsu-Tiamat (Mesopotamian), the Deep (Biblical), cosmic ocean (Hindu)
nodes.symbolism: the state before differentiation, the unconscious from which consciousness emerges, creative potential preceding form
nodes.neumann_archetype: the uroboric state of undifferentiated wholeness, the Great Round as primordial ocean
